+import { test, describe, beforeEach, afterEach } from "node:test";
+import assert from "node:assert/strict";
+import { DiscountedUCB1Bandit } from "../src/bandit.mjs";
+
+/**
+ * @fileoverview Unit tests for Step 7: Feedback recording, reward calculation,
+ * error classification, and database logging in src/bandit.mjs and src/index.mjs.
+ */
+describe("Step 7: Feedback Recording, Reward Calculation, Error Classification & Database Logging", () => {
+  let bandit;
+
+  beforeEach(() => {
+    bandit = new DiscountedUCB1Bandit(":memory:");
+  });
+
+  afterEach(() => {
+    if (bandit && typeof bandit.close === "function") {
+      bandit.close();
+    }
+  });
+
+  describe("Error Classification (_classifyError)", () => {
+    /**
+     * @test Verify ban-provider action for 403 account disabled / banned
+     */
+    test("classifies 403 account disabled as ban-provider", () => {
+      const classification = bandit._classifyError({ status: 403, message: "account disabled or banned" }, "test-provider");
+      assert.equal(classification.action, "ban-provider");
+      assert.equal(classification.scope, "provider");
+      assert.equal(classification.reason, "provider-banned");
+    });
+
+    /**
+     * @test Verify ban-model action for 404 model not found
+     */
+    test("classifies 404 model not found as ban-model", () => {
+      const classification = bandit._classifyError({ status: 404, message: "model does not exist or not found" }, "test-provider");
+      assert.equal(classification.action, "ban-model");
+      assert.equal(classification.scope, "model");
+      assert.equal(classification.reason, "model-not-found");
+    });
+
+    /**
+     * @test Verify cooldown-provider action for 429 quota exhausted
+     */
+    test("classifies 429 quota exhausted as cooldown-provider", () => {
+      const classification = bandit._classifyError({ status: 429, message: "quota exceeded reset after 10m" }, "test-provider");
+      assert.equal(classification.action, "cooldown-provider");
+      assert.equal(classification.reason, "quota-exhausted");
+      assert.equal(classification.cooldownMs, 10 * 60 * 1000);
+    });
+
+    /**
+     * @test Verify cooldown-model action for 5xx server errors
+     */
+    test("classifies 500 server error as cooldown-model", () => {
+      const classification = bandit._classifyError({ status: 500, message: "Internal Server Error" }, "test-provider");
+      assert.equal(classification.action, "cooldown-model");
+      assert.equal(classification.scope, "model");
+      assert.equal(classification.reason, "server-error");
+    });
+
+    /**
+     * @test Verify flag-provider action for 401 auth expired
+     */
+    test("classifies 401 authentication expired as flag-provider", () => {
+      const classification = bandit._classifyError({ status: 401, message: "authentication expired" }, "test-provider");
+      assert.equal(classification.action, "flag-provider");
+      assert.equal(classification.reason, "auth-expired");
+    });
+  });
+
+  describe("Reward Recording & Discounted UCB1 Statistics (recordFeedback)", () => {
+    /**
+     * @test Verify successful feedback updates N, sum_reward, resets fails
+     */
+    test("recordFeedback with success updates N and sum_reward correctly", async () => {
+      bandit.db.prepare("INSERT INTO catalog (id, provider) VALUES (?, ?)").run("test-provider/model-a", "test-provider");
+      await bandit.selectModel();
+
+      const before = bandit.db.prepare("SELECT N, sum_reward, fails FROM models WHERE id = ?").get("test-provider/model-a");
+      assert.equal(before.N, 0);
+
+      bandit.recordFeedback("test-provider/model-a", true, 0.95, null);
+
+      const after = bandit.db.prepare("SELECT N, sum_reward, fails FROM models WHERE id = ?").get("test-provider/model-a");
+      assert.equal(after.N, 1);
+      assert.equal(after.sum_reward, 0.95);
+      assert.equal(after.fails, 0);
+    });
+
+    /**
+     * @test Verify failure feedback increments fails count
+     */
+    test("recordFeedback with failure increments model fails count", async () => {
+      bandit.db.prepare("INSERT INTO catalog (id, provider) VALUES (?, ?)").run("test-provider/model-a", "test-provider");
+      await bandit.selectModel();
+
+      bandit.recordFeedback("test-provider/model-a", false, 0, { status: 502, message: "Bad gateway" });
+
+      const model = bandit.db.prepare("SELECT fails FROM models WHERE id = ?").get("test-provider/model-a");
+      assert.equal(model.fails, 1);
+    });
+  });
+
+  describe("Database Request Logging (request_logs)", () => {
+    /**
+     * @test Verify request_logs stores started_at and ended_at timestamps correctly
+     */
+    test("request_logs records started_at and ended_at timestamps on request lifecycle", async () => {
+      bandit.db.prepare("INSERT INTO catalog (id, provider) VALUES (?, ?)").run("test-provider/model-a", "test-provider");
+      await bandit.selectModel();
+
+      // Simulate starting a request log (as done in index.mjs / bandit methods)
+      bandit.db.prepare("INSERT INTO request_logs (started_at) VALUES (?)").run(Date.now());
+
+      const logBefore = bandit.db.prepare("SELECT * FROM request_logs ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1").get();
+      assert.ok(logBefore);
+      assert.ok(logBefore.started_at > 0);
+      assert.equal(logBefore.ended_at, null);
+
+      // Simulate completing request feedback / logging end
+      bandit.recordFeedback("test-provider/model-a", true, 1.0, null);
+
+      const logAfter = bandit.db.prepare("SELECT * FROM request_logs ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1").get();
+      assert.ok(logAfter);
+      assert.ok(logAfter.ended_at > 0);
+      assert.ok(logAfter.ended_at >= logAfter.started_at);
+    });
+  });
+});

+import { test, describe, beforeEach } from "node:test";
+import assert from "node:assert/strict";
+import {
+  initRegistry,
+  detectProfile,
+  profileMultiplier,
+  listDiscovered,
+  labelDiscovered,
+  dismissDiscovered,
+  registryStats,
+} from "../src/modes-registry.mjs";
+
+// Initialize registry before running tests
+initRegistry();
+
+describe("Modes Registry & Profiling", () => {
+  test("detectProfile: empty or whitespace system prompt returns empty source", () => {
+    const res1 = detectProfile("");
+    assert.equal(res1.mode, "enhance-prompt");
+    assert.equal(res1.profile, "general");
+    assert.equal(res1.source, "empty");
+
+    const res2 = detectProfile("   ");
+    assert.equal(res2.source, "empty");
+  });
+
+  test("detectProfile: pattern match correctly identifies mode and profile", () => {
+    const res = detectProfile("You are a jest test engineer specializing in testing.");
+    assert.equal(res.mode, "jest-test-engineer");
+    assert.equal(res.profile, "code");
+    assert.equal(res.source, "pattern");
+    assert.ok(res.sig);
+  });
+
+  test("detectProfile: signature cache hit on subsequent calls", () => {
+    const prompt = "You are a software architect designing scalable microservices.";
+    const first = detectProfile(prompt);
+    assert.equal(first.source, "pattern");
+
+    const second = detectProfile(prompt);
+    assert.equal(second.source, "signature");
+    assert.equal(second.mode, first.mode);
+    assert.equal(second.profile, first.profile);
+    assert.equal(second.sig, first.sig);
+  });
+
+  test("detectProfile: unknown system prompt triggers discovery", () => {
+    const uniquePrompt = `Unknown custom system prompt test ${Date.now()}`;
+    const res = detectProfile(uniquePrompt);
+    assert.equal(res.mode, null);
+    assert.equal(res.profile, "generic");
+    assert.equal(res.source, "unknown");
+    assert.ok(res.sig);
+
+    const stats = registryStats();
+    assert.ok(stats.discovered >= 1);
+  });
+
+  test("profileMultiplier: generic or empty returns 1.0", () => {
+    assert.equal(profileMultiplier("generic", "gpt-4"), 1.0);
+    assert.equal(profileMultiplier("code", null), 1.0);
+    assert.equal(profileMultiplier(null, "codestral"), 1.0);
+  });
+
+  test("profileMultiplier: FIM model returns 0.3", () => {
+    assert.equal(profileMultiplier("code", "deepseek-coder-fim"), 0.3);
+    assert.equal(profileMultiplier("summarizer", "qwen-fill-in-middle"), 0.3);
+  });
+
+  test("profileMultiplier: code profile boosts code models and penalizes thinking/small models", () => {
+    // Code profile multipliers: codeBoost: 1.35, thinkingPenalty: 0.65, smallPenalty: 0.75
+    const multiplierCode = profileMultiplier("code", "deepseek-coder");
+    assert.ok(multiplierCode > 1.0, "code model should get codeBoost");
+
+    const multiplierThinking = profileMultiplier("code", "deepseek-r1-thinking");
+    assert.ok(multiplierThinking < 1.0, "thinking model should get thinkingPenalty in code profile");
+  });
+
+  test("profileMultiplier: summarizer profile penalizes big/thinking models and boosts fast models", () => {
+    // summarizer: fastBoost: 2.5, notFastPenalty: 0.25, bigPenalty: 0.15, thinkingPenalty: 0.1, codePenalty: 0.5, smallPenalty: 0.9, tpmLowPenalty: 0.05
+    const multiplierFast = profileMultiplier("summarizer", "gemini-3-flash");
+    assert.ok(multiplierFast > 1.0, "fast model gets boosted for summarizer");
+
+    const multiplierBig = profileMultiplier("summarizer", "gpt-5.2-pro");
+    assert.ok(multiplierBig < 1.0, "big model gets penalized for summarizer");
+  });
+
+  test("discovery lifecycle: list, label, and dismiss", () => {
+    const prompt = `Lifecycle test prompt ${Math.random()}`;
+    const detected = detectProfile(prompt);
+    assert.equal(detected.source, "unknown");
+
+    const discoveredList = listDiscovered();
+    const found = discoveredList.find(d => d.sig === detected.sig);
+    assert.ok(found);
+
+    // Label it
+    const labelResult = labelDiscovered(detected.sig, "custom-mode", "code");
+    assert.equal(labelResult.ok, true);
+
+    // Verify it's now in signature cache
+    const reDetected = detectProfile(prompt);
+    assert.equal(reDetected.source, "signature");
+    assert.equal(reDetected.mode, "custom-mode");
+    assert.equal(reDetected.profile, "code");
+
+    // Dismiss another unknown prompt
+    const prompt2 = `Another unknown prompt ${Math.random()}`;
+    const det2 = detectProfile(prompt2);
+    assert.equal(det2.source, "unknown");
+    const dismissed = dismissDiscovered(det2.sig);
+    assert.equal(dismissed, true);
+  });
+});

+import { test, describe, beforeEach } from "node:test";
+import assert from "node:assert/strict";
+import { sessionBlacklist } from "../src/index.mjs";
+
+describe("Nuanced Session Affinity Banning (`__tests__/session-affinity-nuanced.test.mjs`)", () => {
+  beforeEach(() => {
+    sessionBlacklist.clear();
+  });
+
+  test("does not ban model on 1 or 2 transient failures, but bans on 3rd failure or severe failure", () => {
+    const sessionKey = "test_nuanced_session_1";
+    const modelId = "openai/gpt-4o";
+
+    let bl = sessionBlacklist.get(sessionKey);
+    if (!bl) {
+      bl = new Map();
+      sessionBlacklist.set(sessionKey, bl);
+    }
+
+    // Simulate failure 1 (transient)
+    let record = bl.get(modelId);
+    if (!record || typeof record === "number") {
+      record = { fails: typeof record === "number" ? record : 0, severe: false, lastReason: "" };
+      bl.set(modelId, record);
+    }
+    record.fails += 1;
+    record.lastReason = "transient error 502";
+
+    let isBanned = record.severe || record.fails >= 3;
+    assert.equal(isBanned, false, "Model should not be banned after 1 transient failure");
+
+    // Simulate failure 2 (transient)
+    record.fails += 1;
+    record.lastReason = "transient error 503";
+    isBanned = record.severe || record.fails >= 3;
+    assert.equal(isBanned, false, "Model should not be banned after 2 transient failures");
+
+    // Simulate failure 3 (reaches threshold)
+    record.fails += 1;
+    record.lastReason = "transient error 500";
+    isBanned = record.severe || record.fails >= 3;
+    assert.equal(isBanned, true, "Model should be banned after 3 failures");
+  });
+
+  test("immediately bans model on severe error (e.g. status 400 or context window)", () => {
+    const sessionKey = "test_nuanced_session_2";
+    const modelId = "anthropic/claude-3.5-sonnet";
+
+    let bl = sessionBlacklist.get(sessionKey);
+    if (!bl) {
+      bl = new Map();
+      sessionBlacklist.set(sessionKey, bl);
+    }
+
+    let record = bl.get(modelId);
+    if (!record || typeof record === "number") {
+      record = { fails: typeof record === "number" ? record : 0, severe: false, lastReason: "" };
+      bl.set(modelId, record);
+    }
+    record.fails += 1;
+    record.lastReason = "status 400 context window exceeded";
+    record.severe = true;
+
+    const isBanned = record.severe || record.fails >= 3;
+    assert.equal(isBanned, true, "Model should be immediately banned on severe status 400 error even on 1st failure");
+  });
+});

+import { test, describe, beforeEach, afterEach } from "node:test";
+import assert from "node:assert/strict";
+import {
+  computeSessionKey,
+  sessionModels,
+  sessionBlacklist,
+  SESSION_TTL_MS,
+} from "../src/index.mjs";
+
+describe("Session Affinity & Caching Mechanism (`src/index.mjs`)", () => {
+  beforeEach(() => {
+    sessionModels.clear();
+    sessionBlacklist.clear();
+  });
+
+  afterEach(() => {
+    sessionModels.clear();
+    sessionBlacklist.clear();
+  });
+
+  describe("computeSessionKey() Key Generation", () => {
+    /**
+     * @test Verify valid system prompt and user message generate expected 16-char hex MD5 key
+     */
+    test("generates stable 16-char hex MD5 key for valid system and user messages", () => {
+      const messages = [
+        { role: "system", content: "You are Zoo Code assistant." },
+        { role: "user", content: "Write a function to add two numbers." },
+      ];
+      const key1 = computeSessionKey(messages);
+      const key2 = computeSessionKey(messages);
+
+      assert.ok(key1, "Key should not be null");
+      assert.equal(typeof key1, "string");
+      assert.equal(key1.length, 16);
+      assert.equal(key1, key2, "Keys for identical messages should be deterministic");
+    });
+
+    /**
+     * @test Verify handling of missing system prompt or user message (negative / edge cases)
+     */
+    test("returns null when messages array is empty or lacks system/user roles", () => {
+      assert.equal(computeSessionKey([]), null);
+      assert.equal(computeSessionKey("not an array"), null);
+      assert.equal(computeSessionKey([{ role: "assistant", content: "hello" }]), null);
+    });
+
+    /**
+     * @test Verify non-string content (e.g. object/array content) is serialized correctly
+     */
+    test("handles non-string content in messages via JSON serialization", () => {
+      const messages = [
+        { role: "system", content: { text: "system prompt object" } },
+        { role: "user", content: [{ type: "text", text: "user prompt object" }] },
+      ];
+      const key = computeSessionKey(messages);
+      assert.ok(key);
+      assert.equal(key.length, 16);
+    });
+  });
+
+  describe("Session TTL Expiration & Cleanup", () => {
+    /**
+     * @test Verify session entries within TTL are active, while expired entries are removed
+     */
+    test("recognizes active session within TTL and discards expired session", () => {
+      const sessionKey = "testsessionkey12";
+      const modelId = "openai/gpt-4o";
+
+      // Insert fresh session
+      sessionModels.set(sessionKey, { model: modelId, ts: Date.now() });
+
+      const entryFresh = sessionModels.get(sessionKey);
+      assert.ok(entryFresh);
+      assert.equal(Date.now() - entryFresh.ts < SESSION_TTL_MS, true, "Fresh session should be within TTL");
+
+      // Insert expired session (> 30 min ago)
+      const expiredTs = Date.now() - (SESSION_TTL_MS + 1000);
+      sessionModels.set(sessionKey, { model: modelId, ts: expiredTs });
+
+      const entryExpired = sessionModels.get(sessionKey);
+      const isExpired = entryExpired && (Date.now() - entryExpired.ts) >= SESSION_TTL_MS;
+      assert.equal(isExpired, true, "Session should be identified as expired");
+
+      if (isExpired) {
+        sessionModels.delete(sessionKey);
+      }
+      assert.equal(sessionModels.has(sessionKey), false);
+    });
+  });
+
+  describe("LRU Eviction (Max 10k Entries)", () => {
+    /**
+     * @test Verify LRU eviction triggers when sessionModels exceeds 10,000 entries
+     */
+    test("evicts oldest entry when sessionModels exceeds 10,000 entries", () => {
+      // Temporarily populate up to max
+      const oldestKey = "oldest_session_key";
+      sessionModels.set(oldestKey, { model: "model-1", ts: Date.now() });
+
+      // Fill up to 10000 more entries
+      for (let i = 0; i < 10000; i++) {
+        sessionModels.set(`key_${i}`, { model: "model-2", ts: Date.now() });
+      }
+
+      assert.equal(sessionModels.size, 10001);
+
+      // Trigger LRU eviction check implemented in index.mjs
+      if (sessionModels.size > 10000) {
+        const firstKey = sessionModels.keys().next().value;
+        sessionModels.delete(firstKey);
+        sessionBlacklist.delete(firstKey);
+      }
+
+      assert.equal(sessionModels.size, 10000);
+      assert.equal(sessionModels.has(oldestKey), false, "Oldest entry should be evicted");
+    });
+  });
+
+  describe("Model Failure Invalidation", () => {
+    /**
+     * @test Verify session model pin is invalidated and removed upon model failure
+     */
+    test("invalidates session pin on model failure", () => {
+      const sessionKey = "invalidation_test_key";
+      const modelId = "anthropic/claude-3.5-sonnet";
+
+      sessionModels.set(sessionKey, { model: modelId, ts: Date.now() });
+      assert.equal(sessionModels.has(sessionKey), true);
+
+      // Simulate model failure handling (unpin / delete sessionModels)
+      const entry = sessionModels.get(sessionKey);
+      if (entry && entry.model === modelId) {
+        sessionModels.delete(sessionKey);
+      }
+
+      assert.equal(sessionModels.has(sessionKey), false, "Session pin should be deleted on model failure");
+    });
+  });
+});

+import { test, describe } from "node:test";
+import assert from "node:assert/strict";
+import { DiscountedUCB1Bandit } from "../src/bandit.mjs";
+import { compressBody, truncateBiggestMessage } from "../src/index.mjs";
+
+const bandit = new DiscountedUCB1Bandit(":memory:");
+
+describe("Step 5: Token Estimation, Context Compression & Body Preparation", () => {
+  describe("Token Estimation (estimateTokens)", () => {
+    /**
+     * @test Verify estimateTokens uses ~4 chars/token heuristic for strings
+     */
+    test("estimates tokens using ~4 chars/token heuristic for string content", () => {
+      const body = {
+        messages: [
+          { role: "system", content: "12345678" }, // 8 chars -> 2 tokens
+          { role: "user", content: "123456789012" } // 12 chars -> 3 tokens
+        ]
+      };
+      // Total chars = 20. Math.ceil(20 / 4) = 5
+      assert.equal(bandit.estimateTokens(body), 5);
+    });
+
+    /**
+     * @test Verify multimodal content handling (text parts and image_url heuristic divided by 4)
+     */
+    test("handles multimodal content with text and image_url", () => {
+      const body = {
+        messages: [
+          {
+            role: "user",
+            content: [
+              { type: "text", text: "Hello" }, // 5 chars
+              { type: "image_url", image_url: { url: "http://..." } } // +1000 chars heuristic
+            ]
+          }
+        ]
+      };
+      // Total chars = 1005. Math.ceil(1005 / 4) = 252
+      assert.equal(bandit.estimateTokens(body), 252);
+    });
+
+    /**
+     * @test Verify non-string/non-array content fallback via JSON serialization
+     */
+    test("handles non-string/non-array content via JSON serialization fallback", () => {
+      const body = {
+        messages: [
+          { role: "assistant", content: { foo: "bar" } }
+        ]
+      };
+      const jsonStr = JSON.stringify({ foo: "bar" });
+      const expectedTokens = Math.ceil(jsonStr.length / 4);
+      assert.equal(bandit.estimateTokens(body), expectedTokens);
+    });
+
+    /**
+     * @test Verify 0 tokens returned for invalid or empty body
+     */
+    test("returns 0 for empty or invalid body", () => {
+      assert.equal(bandit.estimateTokens(null), 0);
+      assert.equal(bandit.estimateTokens({}), 0);
+    });
+  });
+
+  describe("Emergency Truncation (truncateBiggestMessage)", () => {
+    /**
+     * @test Verify null returned for empty or invalid body
+     */
+    test("returns null if messages length is 0 or body is invalid", () => {
+      assert.equal(truncateBiggestMessage(null, 1000), null);
+      assert.equal(truncateBiggestMessage({ messages: [] }, 1000), null);
+    });
+
+    /**
+     * @test Verify proportional truncation of the largest message when tokens >= 2000
+     */
+    test("truncates biggest message when tokens >= 2000 and total exceeds target", () => {
+      const largeContent = "A".repeat(10000); // ~3333 tokens
+      const body = {
+        messages: [
+          { role: "system", content: "You are a helpful assistant." },
+          { role: "user", content: largeContent }
+        ]
+      };
+      const result = truncateBiggestMessage(body, 1000);
+      assert.ok(result);
+      assert.equal(result.truncatedBig, true);
+      assert.ok(result.body.messages[1].content.includes("[... troncato:"));
+    });
+  });
+
+  describe("Sliding Window Compression (compressBody)", () => {
+    /**
+     * @test Verify null returned for invalid body
+     */
+    test("returns null for invalid body", () => {
+      assert.equal(compressBody(null, 1000), null);
+      assert.equal(compressBody({ messages: [] }, 1000), null);
+    });
+
+    /**
+     * @test Verify messages < 6 fallback to truncateBiggestMessage
+     */
+    test("falls back to truncateBiggestMessage when messages < 6", () => {
+      const body = {
+        messages: [
+          { role: "system", content: "Sys" },
+          { role: "user", content: "A".repeat(12000) }
+        ]
+      };
+      const result = compressBody(body, 500);
+      assert.ok(result);
+      assert.equal(result.truncatedBig, true);
+    });
+
+    /**
+     * @test Verify sliding window compression (system + first user + tail + summary) when messages >= 6
+     */
+    test("applies sliding window compression when messages >= 6", () => {
+      const messages = [
+        { role: "system", content: "System prompt" },
+        { role: "user", content: "First user question" },
+        { role: "assistant", content: "Response 1" },
+        { role: "user", content: "Question 2" },
+        { role: "assistant", content: "Response 2" },
+        { role: "user", content: "Question 3" },
+        { role: "assistant", content: "Response 3" },
+        { role: "user", content: "Question 4" },
+        { role: "assistant", content: "Response 4" },
+        { role: "user", content: "Question 5" },
+        { role: "assistant", content: "Response 5" },
+        { role: "user", content: "Final question" }
+      ];
+      const body = { messages };
+      const result = compressBody(body, 50000);
+      assert.ok(result);
+      assert.ok(result.body.messages.length < messages.length);
+      assert.equal(result.body.messages[0].role, "system");
+      assert.equal(result.body.messages[1].role, "user");
+      assert.equal(result.body.messages[1].content, "First user question");
+      
+      const summaryMsg = result.body.messages.find(m => typeof m.content === "string" && m.content.includes("messaggi intermedi omessi"));
+      assert.ok(summaryMsg);
+    });
+  });
+
+  describe("Tool Dropping on Summarization Requests", () => {
+    /**
+     * @test Verify tools, tool_choice, and parallel_tool_calls are dropped when summarization is detected
+     */
+    test("drops tools when summarization request is detected", () => {
+      const body = {
+        messages: [
+          { role: "system", content: "System instructions" },
+          { role: "user", content: "Please summarize our conversation without calling any tools." }
+        ],
+        tools: [{ type: "function", function: { name: "test_tool" } }],
+        tool_choice: "auto",
+        parallel_tool_calls: true
+      };
+
+      const firstMsg = body.messages[0]?.content || "";
+      const firstMsgStr = typeof firstMsg === "string" ? firstMsg : JSON.stringify(firstMsg);
+      const isSummarization = /summariz|summariz|condense|context.*compress|riassunt/i.test(firstMsgStr.slice(0, 500)) ||
+        /summariz|summariz|condense|context.*compress|riassunt/i.test((body.messages[1]?.content || "").slice(0, 500));
+
+      const hasTools = Array.isArray(body.tools) && body.tools.length > 0;
+      if (hasTools && isSummarization) {
+        delete body.tools;
+        delete body.tool_choice;
+        delete body.parallel_tool_calls;
+      }
+
+      assert.equal(body.tools, undefined);
+      assert.equal(body.tool_choice, undefined);
+      assert.equal(body.parallel_tool_calls, undefined);
+    });
+  });
+});

+    /**
+     * @test Verify excludedModels Set correctly tracks failed model/provider pairs

+    test("excludedModels Set tracks failed models across attempts", () => {

+      const failedModel = "provider1/model-a";
+

+      excluded.add(failedModel);
+      assert.equal(excluded.has(failedModel), true);
+      assert.equal(excluded.size, 1);

+      const streamMaxMs = parseInt(process.env.STREAM_MAX_MS || "180000", 10);
+
+      assert.equal(typeof upstreamTimeoutMs, "number");
+      assert.equal(upstreamTimeoutMs > 0, true);
+
+      assert.equal(typeof streamIdleMs, "number");
+      assert.equal(streamIdleMs > 0, true);
+
+      assert.equal(typeof streamMaxMs, "number");
+      assert.equal(streamMaxMs > 0, true);
+    });
+  });
+
+  describe("Fallback Models Chain", () => {
+    /**
+     * @test Verify fallback models retrieval and filtering
+     */
+    test("retrieves fallback models and filters correctly", () => {
+      const fallbackModels = bandit.getFallbackModels();
+      assert.ok(Array.isArray(fallbackModels));
+
+      const fallbackTried = new Set();
+      for (const fallbackModel of fallbackModels) {
+        if (!fallbackTried.has(fallbackModel) && bandit.isModelAvailable(fallbackModel)) {
+          fallbackTried.add(fallbackModel);
+          assert.ok(typeof fallbackModel === "string");
+          break;
+        }
+      }
+    });

+# Plan: Fix Model Selection, Enhance Prompt, and Dashboard Metrics
+
+## Overview
+This plan addresses issues where no model is selected during proxy chat/enhance requests, enhance prompt requests fail, and dashboard metrics need analysis and restoration.
+
+## Alternative Sources Investigated
+1. **Catalog Seeding & Environment Filtering**: Empty catalog or overly restrictive environment filters (`ONLY_FREE`, `EXCLUDE_PAID`, `EXCLUDE_THINKING`) eliminating all models in [`src/bandit.mjs`](src/bandit.mjs:1077).
+2. **Session Affinity Stale State**: Stale or permanently banned models stored in session caches in [`src/index.mjs`](src/index.mjs:1015).
+3. **Enhance Prompt Profile Detection**: System prompt signature / pattern matching failing in [`src/modes-registry.mjs`](src/modes-registry.mjs:60).
+4. **Database Table / Query Failures**: Missing `request_logs` columns or SQL errors in `getDashboardStats()` in [`src/bandit.mjs`](src/bandit.mjs:965).
+5. **Dashboard Auth & API Endpoints**: Authentication token header mismatch or response format issues in [`public/dashboard.html`](public/dashboard.html:703) and [`src/index.mjs`](src/index.mjs:694).
+
+## Architecture / Workflow Diagram
+
+```mermaid
+graph TD
+    Client[Client Request] --> Proxy[Proxy Endpoint /v1/chat/completions]
+    Proxy --> Select[Bandit selectModel]
+    Select --> Check[Filter Catalog and DB Models]
+    Check --> Forward[Forward to Upstream]
+    Forward --> Feedback[Record Feedback]
+    Dashboard[Dashboard Frontend] --> StatsAPI[/v1/dashboard/stats]
+    Dashboard --> MetricsAPI[/v1/metrics]
+```
+
+## Actionable Steps
+1. **Model Selection & Filtering Review**:
+   - Inspect catalog loading and filter logic in [`src/bandit.mjs`](src/bandit.mjs:1077).
+   - Ensure fallback models and session affinity handle unavailable models gracefully.
+2. **Enhance Prompt Handling**:
+   - Verify `detectProfile()` and system prompt processing in [`src/modes-registry.mjs`](src/modes-registry.mjs:60) and [`src/index.mjs`](src/index.mjs:1111).
+3. **Dashboard Metrics Restoration**:

+   - Check API authentication and rendering logic in [`public/dashboard.html`](public/dashboard.html:703).
+4. **Verification**:
+   - Run tests and verify server metrics.

+import http from 'node:http';
+import { spawn } from 'node:child_process';
+import assert from 'node:assert';
+
+async function main() {
+  // 1. Start mock upstream server on ephemeral port (0)
+  const upstreamServer = http.createServer((req, res) => {
+    if (req.method === 'GET' && req.url === '/v1/models') {
+      res.writeHead(200, { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' });
+      res.end(JSON.stringify({
+        data: [
+          {
+            id: 'mistral/mistral-small-latest',
+            provider: 'mistral',
+            max_input_tokens: 32000,
+            is_free: 1,
+            supports_tools: 1
+          }
+        ]
+      }));
+    } else if (req.method === 'POST' && req.url === '/v1/chat/completions') {
+      let body = '';
+      req.on('data', chunk => body += chunk);
+      req.on('end', () => {
+        res.writeHead(200, { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' });
+        res.end(JSON.stringify({
+          id: 'chatcmpl-mock',
+          object: 'chat.completion',
+          created: Date.now(),
+          model: 'mistral/mistral-small-latest',
+          choices: [{
+            index: 0,
+            message: {
+              role: 'assistant',
+              content: 'Hello from mock upstream!'
+            },
+            finish_reason: 'stop'
+          }],
+          usage: { prompt_tokens: 5, completion_tokens: 6, total_tokens: 11 }
+        }));
+      });
+    } else {
+      res.writeHead(404);
+      res.end('Not found: ' + req.method + ' ' + req.url);
+    }
+  });
+
+  await new Promise(resolve => upstreamServer.listen(0, '127.0.0.1', resolve));
+  const upstreamPort = upstreamServer.address().port;
+  const upstreamUrl = `http://127.0.0.1:${upstreamPort}/v1`;
+  console.log(`[TEST] Mock upstream running on ${upstreamUrl}`);
+
+  // 2. Start proxy server in background
+  const proxyProcess = spawn('npm', ['start'], {
+    env: { ...process.env, PORT: '8081', OMNIROUTE_BASE_URL: upstreamUrl, HEALTH_CHECK_ENABLED: 'false' },
+    stdio: 'inherit'
+  });
+
+  // Wait for proxy to start and sync models
+  await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 3500));
+
+  try {
+    console.log('[TEST] Sending POST /v1/chat/completions to proxy on http://127.0.0.1:8081...');
+    const response = await fetch('http://127.0.0.1:8081/v1/chat/completions', {
+      method: 'POST',
+      headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
+      body: JSON.stringify({
+        model: 'mistral/mistral-small-latest',
+        messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Hello proxy!' }]
+      })
+    });
+
+    console.log('[TEST] Response status:', response.status);
+    assert.equal(response.status, 200, 'Expected status 200 OK');
+
+    const data = await response.json();
+    console.log('[TEST] Response body:', JSON.stringify(data, null, 2));
+    assert.ok(data.choices && data.choices.length > 0, 'Expected choices in response');
+    assert.equal(data.choices[0].message.content, 'Hello from mock upstream!');
+
+    console.log('[TEST] SUCCESS: Final verification request completed successfully!');
+  } finally {
+    proxyProcess.kill();
+    upstreamServer.close();
+  }
+}
+
+main().catch(err => {
+  console.error('[TEST] ERROR:', err);
+  process.exit(1);
+});

+const activeRequests = new Map();

+  activeRequests.set(id, {

+    startTime: Date.now(),

+export function trackRequestUpdate(id, patch) {
+  const r = activeRequests.get(id);

+export function trackRequestEnd(id) {
+  activeRequests.delete(id);

+  return activeRequests.size;

+import test from "node:test";
+import assert from "node:assert";
+import { DiscountedUCB1Bandit } from "../src/bandit.mjs";
+
+function makeBandit() {
+  return new DiscountedUCB1Bandit(":memory:");
+}
+
+function seedCatalog(bandit, modelId, provider, maxInput = 8000, isFree = 1, supportsTools = 1) {
+  bandit.db.prepare(`
+    INSERT OR REPLACE INTO catalog (id, provider, max_input_tokens, is_free, supports_tools)
+    VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
+  `).run(modelId, provider, maxInput, isFree, supportsTools);
+}
+
+test("selectModel: relaxation strategy recovers when token limits exceed all models", async () => {
+  const b = makeBandit();
+  // Model with small max_input_tokens (8000)
+  seedCatalog(b, "p1/small-model", "p1", 8000, 1, 1);
+
+  // Request estimatedTokens = 100000 (exceeds 8000 * 1.1)
+  const chosen = await b.selectModel(new Set(), 100000, false);
+  
+  // Without relaxation, this would return null. With relaxation tier 1, it should recover and select p1/small-model.
+  assert.equal(chosen, "p1/small-model");
+});
+
+test("selectModel: relaxation strategy recovers when policy (onlyFree / excludePaid) filters all models", async () => {
+  const b = makeBandit();
+  // Seed a paid model (is_free = 0)
+  seedCatalog(b, "p1/paid-model", "p1", 128000, 0, 1);
+
+  // Set onlyFree = true
+  b.onlyFree = true;
+
+  const chosen = await b.selectModel();
+  
+  // Without relaxation, this would return null. With relaxation tier 2, it recovers.
+  assert.equal(chosen, "p1/paid-model");
+});

+test("_parseResetAfter: handles HTTP-date and header formats", () => {
+  const b = makeBandit();
+  // Header as numeric string seconds
+  assert.equal(b._parseResetAfter("", { retryAfter: "45" }), 45000);
+  // Header as number seconds
+  assert.equal(b._parseResetAfter("", { retry_after: 120 }), 120000);
+  // Header object with get()
+  const mockHeaders = { get: (name) => name === 'retry-after' ? '30' : null };
+  assert.equal(b._parseResetAfter("", { headers: mockHeaders }), 30000);
+  // HTTP-date future date
+  const futureDate = new Date(Date.now() + 60000).toUTCString();

+});

+git_cmd_capture() {
+    if [[ "$DRY_RUN" == "true" ]]; then
+        echo "[DRY RUN] $*" >&2
+        # For dry run, we still need to return something reasonable for capture
+        # Return empty string for most commands, or simulate expected output
+        case "$1" in
+            "git diff --name-only")
+                echo ""  # No changes in dry run
+                ;;
+            "git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD")
+                echo "HEAD"  # Simulate current branch
+                ;;
+            "git diff --cached --name-only")
+                echo ""  # No staged changes in dry run
+                ;;
+            "git diff --cached --stat --name-only")
+                echo ""  # No stats in dry run
+                ;;
+            *)
+                echo ""  # Default empty response
+                ;;
+        esac
         return 0
     fi
+    eval "$@"

+# Fix Git extension interference
+fix_git_extension_interference() {
+    log_info "Checking for Git extension interference..."
+
+    # Disable fsmonitor if it's causing issues
+    if git_cmd_capture "git config --get core.fsmonitor" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+        log_warn "fsmonitor is enabled, which may cause interference"
+        if [[ "$DRY_RUN" != "true" ]]; then
+            git_cmd "git config --unset core.fsmonitor" >/dev/null 2>&1
+            log_info "Disabled fsmonitor configuration"
+        else
+            log_info "[DRY RUN] Would disable fsmonitor configuration"
+        fi
+    fi
+
+    # Ensure fileMode is properly set (especially important on WSL)
+    local filemode
+    filemode=$(git_cmd_capture "git config --get core.filemode" 2>/dev/null || echo "unset")
+    if [[ "$filemode" != "false" ]]; then
+        # On WSL, we often want to ignore file mode changes
+        log_info "Setting core.filemode to false to ignore permission changes"
+        if [[ "$DRY_RUN" != "true" ]]; then
+            git_cmd "git config core.filemode false" >/dev/null 2>&1
+        else
+            log_info "[DRY RUN] Would set core.filemode to false"
+        fi
+    fi
+
+    # Check for GitKraken or other GUI interference
+    # This is more of a informational check
+    if [[ -d ".git/gitkraken" ]] || [[ -f ".git/gitkraken.conf" ]]; then
+        log_warn "GitKraken metadata detected in repository"
+    fi

+    return 0

+# Check for secrets in staged changes
+check_secrets() {
+    log_info "Checking for secrets in staged changes..."
+
+    # Get list of staged files
+    local staged_files
+    staged_files=$(git_cmd_capture "git diff --cached --name-only" 2>/dev/null || true)
+
+    if [[ -z "$staged_files" ]]; then
+        log_debug "No staged files to check for secrets"
+        return 0
+    fi
+
+    # Patterns for common secrets
+    local secret_patterns=(
+        'password\s*=\s*[^[:space:]]+'
+        'api_key\s*=\s*[^[:space:]]+'
+        'secret\s*=\s*[^[:space:]]+'
+        'key\s*=\s*[^[:space:]]+'
+        'token\s*=\s*[^[:space:]]+'
+        '-----BEGIN [A-Z]+ PRIVATE KEY-----'
+        'ssh-rsa AAAAB3NzaC1yc2E'
+        'ssh-dss AAAAB3NzaC1kc3'
+        'ecdsa-sha2-nistp256 AAAAE2VjZHNhLXNoYTItbmlzdHAyNTYAAAAIbmlzdHAyNTYAAABBBB'
+    )
+
+    local found_secret=0
+    local secret_file=""
+
+    while IFS= read -r file; do
+        [[ -z "$file" ]] && continue
+
+        # Exclude git-utils.sh from secret checks to avoid false positives
+        if [[ "$file" == *"git-utils.sh" ]]; then
+            continue
+        fi
+
+        # Check if file exists
+        if [[ ! -f "$file" ]]; then
+            continue
+        fi
+
+        # Check for secret patterns in the staged version of the file
+        local staged_content
+        staged_content=$(git_cmd_capture "git show :$file" 2>/dev/null || true)
+
+        if [[ -n "$staged_content" ]]; then
+            for pattern in "${secret_patterns[@]}"; do
+                if echo "$staged_content" | grep -iqE -e "$pattern" 2>/dev/null; then
+                    log_warn "Potential secret found in file: $file"
+                    found_secret=1
+                    secret_file="$file"
+                    break
+                fi
+            done
+        fi
+
+        if [[ $found_secret -eq 1 ]]; then
+            break
+        fi
+    done <<< "$staged_files"
+
+    if [[ $found_secret -eq 1 ]]; then
+        log_error "Secret detected in $secret_file. Commit aborted to prevent leaking credentials."
         return 1
+    else
+        log_info "No secrets detected in staged changes"
+        return 0
     fi

@@ -0,0 +1,35 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+import sys
+
+def find_conflict_markers(file_path):
+    try:
+        with open(file_path, 'r') as f:
+            lines = f.readlines()
+
+        conflict_lines = []
+        for i, line in enumerate(lines, 1):
+            if line.startswith('<<<<<<<') or line.startswith('=======') or line.startswith('>>>>>>>'):
+                conflict_lines.append((i, line.rstrip()))
+
+        if conflict_lines:
+            print("Conflict markers found:")
+            for line_num, line_content in conflict_lines:
+                print(f"Line {line_num}: {line_content}")
+            return True
+        else:
+            print("No conflict markers found.")
+            return False
+    except FileNotFoundError:
+        print(f"File not found: {file_path}")
+        return False
+    except Exception as e:
+        print(f"Error reading file: {e}")
+        return False
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    if len(sys.argv) != 2:
+        print("Usage: python find_conflicts.py <file_path>")
+        sys.exit(1)
+
+    file_path = sys.argv[1]
+    find_conflict_markers(file_path)

+  async resolveModelPrefix(modelId) {
+    // Already has explicit provider prefix
+    if (modelId.includes('/')) return modelId;
+
+    // Special static model resolution
+    if (modelId === 'static-best-free') {
+      return await this.getBestFreeModel();
+    }
+
+    // Search the catalog for an exact match on the full id
+    const exact = this.db.prepare("SELECT id FROM catalog WHERE id = ?").get(modelId);
+    if (exact) {
+      return exact.id;
+    }
+
+    // Search for model part match: extract model name from id (after the '/')
+    const catalogMatch = this.db.prepare(
+      "SELECT id FROM catalog WHERE substr(id, instr(id, '/') + 1) = ?"
+    ).get(modelId);
+
+    if (catalogMatch) {
+      return catalogMatch.id;
+    }
+
+    // Search the models table too
+    const modelsMatch = this.db.prepare(
+      "SELECT id FROM models WHERE substr(id, instr(id, '/') + 1) = ?"
+    ).get(modelId);
+
+    if (modelsMatch) {
+      return modelsMatch.id;
+    }
+
+    // Fallback: heuristic parsing
+    return this._getProvider(modelId);
+  }
+
+  async getBestFreeModel() {
+    // Get all free models from the catalog
+    const freeModels = this.db.prepare(
+      `SELECT c.id, c.provider, c.max_input_tokens, c.supports_tools
+       FROM catalog c
+       WHERE c.is_free = 1
+       ORDER BY c.provider, substr(c.id, instr(c.id, '/') + 1)`
+    ).all();
+
+    if (freeModels.length === 0) {
+      return null;
+    }
+
+    // Get performance data for these models from the models table
+    const modelIds = freeModels.map(m => m.id);
+    const placeholders = modelIds.map(() => '?').join(', ');
+    const modelStats = this.db.prepare(
+      `SELECT id, N, sum_reward, fails, cooldown_until, permanent, degraded
+       FROM models
+       WHERE id IN (${placeholders})`
+    ).all(...modelIds);
+
+    // Filter out unavailable models (cooldown, permanent, degraded)
+    const now = Date.now();
+    const availableModels = freeModels.filter(fm => {
+      const stats = modelStats.find(ms => ms.id === fm.id);
+      if (!stats) return true; // Model exists in catalog but not in models table (new model)
+      if (stats.permanent === 1) return false;
+      if (stats.degraded === 1) return false;
+      if (stats.cooldown_until > now) return false;
+      return true;
+    });
+
+    if (availableModels.length === 0) {
+      return null;
+    }
+
+    // Rank by UCB1 average reward (sum_reward / N)
+    const rankedModels = availableModels.map(fm => {
+      const stats = modelStats.find(ms => ms.id === fm.id);
+      const N = stats ? stats.N : 0;
+      const sum_reward = stats ? stats.sum_reward : 0;
+      const avg = N > 0 ? sum_reward / N : 0;
+      return { ...fm, avg, N };
+    });
+
+    // Sort by average reward (descending), then by N (descending for more data)
+    rankedModels.sort((a, b) => {
+      if (b.avg !== a.avg) return b.avg - a.avg;
+      return b.N - a.N;
+    });
+
+    // Return the best available model's full provider/model ID
+    return rankedModels[0].id;
+  }

@@ -0,0 +1,66 @@
+// Script to remove duplicate methods from bandit.mjs
+const fs = require('fs');
+
+// Read the file
+let content = fs.readFileSync('src/bandit.mjs', 'utf8');
+const lines = content.split('\n');
+
+// Define duplicate method ranges to remove (line numbers are 1-based)
+// Format: [startLine, endLine] where endLine is inclusive
+const duplicates = [
+  [802, 811],    // _getProviderCooldownMs duplicate
+  [971, 1050],   // recordFeedback duplicate (from line 971 to just before _parseResetAfter)
+  [1053, 1070],  // _parseResetAfter duplicate
+  [1072, 1081],  // _unlockProvider duplicate
+  [1083, 1091],  // _recordTrainingFeedback duplicate
+  [1094, 1097],  // _recordProviderFailure duplicate
+  [1100, 1105],  // _forceProviderCooldown duplicate
+  [1107, 1114]   // _triggerFallback duplicate
+];
+
+// Sort by start line in descending order so we can remove from bottom to top
+const sortedDuplicates = duplicates.sort((a, b) => b[0] - a[0]);
+
+// Remove duplicates
+let resultLines = lines;
+for (const [start, end] of sortedDuplicates) {
+  // Convert to 0-based indices
+  const startIdx = start - 1;
+  const endIdx = end; // end is inclusive, so we need to remove up to this line
+
+  resultLines = resultLines.filter((_, i) => !(i >= startIdx && i < endIdx));
+}
+
+// Write back the file
+fs.writeFileSync('src/bandit.mjs', resultLines.join('\n'));
+
+console.log('Removed duplicate methods from bandit.mjs');
+
+// Verify by checking for remaining duplicates
+const verifyContent = fs.readFileSync('src/bandit.mjs', 'utf8');
+const verifyLines = verifyContent.split('\n');
+
+// Check for remaining duplicates
+const remainingDuplicates = [];
+for (const [start, end] of duplicates) {
+  // Check if any of these lines still exist
+  for (let i = start - 1; i < Math.min(end, verifyLines.length); i++) {
+    if (verifyLines[i] && verifyLines[i].includes('_getProviderCooldownMs') ||
+        verifyLines[i].includes('recordFeedback') ||
+        verifyLines[i].includes('_parseResetAfter') ||
+        verifyLines[i].includes('_unlockProvider') ||
+        verifyLines[i].includes('_recordTrainingFeedback') ||
+        verifyLines[i].includes('_recordProviderFailure') ||
+        verifyLines[i].includes('_forceProviderCooldown') ||
+        verifyLines[i].includes('_triggerFallback')) {
+      remainingDuplicates.push(start);
+      break;
+    }
+  }
+}
+
+if (remainingDuplicates.length > 0) {
+  console.log('WARNING: Some duplicates may still exist at lines:', remainingDuplicates);
+} else {
+  console.log('All duplicates removed successfully!');
+}

+#!/bin/bash
+cd /home/marco/omniroute-bandit-proxy
+
+# Test cases
+test_cases=(
+    "fix: test message"
+    "feat(scope): add feature"
+    "docs: update readme"
+    "refactor(core): simplify logic"
+    "test: add unit tests"
+    "chore: update dependencies"
+    "style: fix formatting"
+    "invalid: message"
+    "no-colon-message"
+    "feat(scope):"
+    "feat: "
+)
+
+for subject in "${test_cases[@]}"; do
+    # Using a variable for the pattern to avoid issues with quoting
+    pattern='^(feat|fix|docs|style|refactor|test|chore)(\([^)]+\))?:\ .+'
+    if [[ "$subject" =~ $pattern ]]; then
+        echo "\"$subject\" -> MATCH"
+    else
+        echo "\"$subject\" -> NO MATCH"
+    fi
+done

diff --git a/tests/test-fallback-tools-fix.mjs b/tests/test-fallback-tools-fix.mjs

+import { test } from "node:test";
+import assert from "node:assert/strict";
+import Database from "better-sqlite3";
+
+const DB_PATH = "bandit.test-fallback-tools.db";
+
+test("FALLBACK FIX: fallback model selection checks supports_tools when requireTools=true", async () => {
+  // Clean up any previous test database
+  import("node:fs").then(({ existsSync, rmSync }) => {
+    if (existsSync(DB_PATH)) rmSync(DB_PATH);
+  });
+
+  const db = new Database(DB_PATH);
+
+  // Setup: create models and catalog tables with the schema used by the real bandit
+  db.exec(`
+    CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS models (
+      id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
+      provider TEXT,
+      N INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
+      avg REAL DEFAULT 0,
+      sum_reward REAL DEFAULT 0,
+      fails INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
+      cooldown_until INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
+      permanent INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
+      degraded INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
+      dynamic_max_tokens INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
+      consecutive_5xx INTEGER DEFAULT 0
+    );
+    CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS catalog (
+      id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
+      provider TEXT,
+      max_input_tokens INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
+      is_free INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
+      supports_tools INTEGER DEFAULT 0
+    );
+    CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS provider_history (
+      provider TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
+      cooldown_until INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
+      permanent INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
+      attention_flags INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
+      needs_attention INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
+      attention_reason TEXT DEFAULT '',
+      attention_message TEXT DEFAULT ''
+    );
+    CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS meta (
+      key TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
+      value TEXT DEFAULT ''
+    );
+  `);
+
+  // Insert models that are ALL IN COOLDOWN/BAN (so bandit selection returns null)
+  const fallbackModels = [
+    "mistral/ministral-8b-latest",
+    "groq/allam-2-7b",
+    "mistral/mistral-small-latest",
+    "mistral/mistral-large-latest",
+    "groq/llama-3.3-70b-versatile",
+    "openrouter/gpt-oss-20b"
+  ];
+
+  const insertModel = db.prepare(
+    `INSERT INTO models (id, provider, permanent, degraded, cooldown_until) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)`
+  );
+
+  // Make ALL models unavailable so the fallback path is triggered
+  for (const modelId of fallbackModels) {
+    const [id, provider] = modelId.split("/");
+    insertModel.run(id, provider, 0, 0, Date.now() + 1000 * 60 * 60); // 1h cooldown
+  }
+
+  // Insert catalog entries:
+  // - ministral and mistral-small support tools
+  // - allam-2-7b and gpt-oss-20b do NOT support tools
+  const insertCatalog = db.prepare(
+    `INSERT INTO catalog (id, provider, supports_tools) VALUES (?, ?, ?)`
+  );
+
+  insertCatalog.run("mistral/ministral-8b-latest", "mistral", 1); // supports tools
+  insertCatalog.run("groq/allam-2-7b", "groq", 0); // NO tools
+  insertCatalog.run("mistral/mistral-small-latest", "mistral", 1); // supports tools
+  insertCatalog.run("mistral/mistral-large-latest", "mistral", 1); // supports tools
+  insertCatalog.run("groq/llama-3.3-70b-versatile", "groq", 1); // supports tools
+  insertCatalog.run("openrouter/gpt-oss-20b", "openrouter", 0); // NO tools
+
+  // Import index handler to test fallback logic
+  // We simulate the fallback decision by querying the DB the same way index.mjs does
+
+  // Test: when requireTools=true and ALL tool-capable models are unavailable
+  // the fallback should return null (not a non-tool model)
+  let selectedFallbackModel = null;
+  const fallbackTried = new Set();
+
+  const modelIdToSelect = "felo/gpt-oss-20b-tool-use"; // model that failed and triggered fallback
+  const requireTools = true;
+
+  for (const fallbackModel of fallbackModels) {
+    if (fallbackTried.has(fallbackModel)) continue;
+    if (fallbackModel !== modelIdToSelect) {
+      // simulate bandit.isModelAvailable(fallbackModel) -> returns false (all in cooldown)
+      const modelRow = db.prepare("SELECT permanent, degraded, cooldown_until FROM models WHERE id = ?").get(fallbackModel);
+      if (modelRow && (modelRow.permanent === 1 || modelRow.degraded === 1 || (modelRow.cooldown_until && modelRow.cooldown_until > Date.now()))) {
+        continue; // model unavailable
+      }
+      if (requireTools) {
+        const modelInfo = db.prepare("SELECT supports_tools FROM catalog WHERE id = ?").get(fallbackModel);
+        if (!modelInfo || modelInfo.supports_tools !== 1) continue; // doesn't support tools
+      }
+      selectedFallbackModel = fallbackModel;
+      break;
+    }
+  }
+
+  assert.equal(selectedFallbackModel, null, "When all tool-capable fallback models are unavailable, fallback should return null (not select a non-tool-capable model)");
+  console.log("✅ FALLBACK TEST PASSED: Non-tool-capable models are correctly skipped when requireTools=true");
+
+  // Test 2: when at least one tool-capable fallback model IS available, it should be selected
+  // Clear cooldown on one tool-capable model
+  db.prepare("UPDATE models SET cooldown_until = 0 WHERE id = 'mistral/ministral-8b-latest'").run();
+
+  selectedFallbackModel = null;
+  for (const fallbackModel of fallbackModels) {
+    if (fallbackTried.has(fallbackModel)) continue;
+    const modelRow = db.prepare("SELECT permanent, degraded, cooldown_until FROM models WHERE id = ?").get(fallbackModel);
+    if (modelRow && (modelRow.permanent === 1 || modelRow.degraded === 1 || (modelRow.cooldown_until && modelRow.cooldown_until > Date.now()))) {
+      continue;
+    }
+    if (requireTools) {
+      const modelInfo = db.prepare("SELECT supports_tools FROM catalog WHERE id = ?").get(fallbackModel);
+      if (!modelInfo || modelInfo.supports_tools !== 1) continue;
+    }
+    selectedFallbackModel = fallbackModel;
+    break;
+  }
+
+  assert.equal(selectedFallbackModel, "mistral/ministral-8b-latest", "When a tool-capable fallback model is available, it should be selected");
+  console.log("✅ FALLBACK TEST 2 PASSED: Tool-capable fallback model correctly selected when available");
+
+  // Cleanup

+# Fix empty modifications (e.g., permission changes, line ending differences)
+fix_empty_modifications() {
+    log_info "Checking for empty modifications (permission/line-ending changes...)"
+
+    local changed_files
+    changed_files=$(git_cmd_capture "git diff --name-only" 2>/dev/null || true)
+
+    if [[ -z "$changed_files" ]]; then
+        log_debug "No files to check for empty modifications"
+        return 0
+    fi
+
+    local fixed_count=0
+    while IFS= read -r file; do
+        [[ -z "$file" ]] && continue
+
+        # Check if the diff is empty (only whitespace/permission changes)
+        local diff_size
+        diff_size=$(git diff --ignore-all-space -- "$file" 2>/dev/null | wc -c || echo 0)
+
+        if [[ $diff_size -le 5 ]]; then
+            # Likely just line ending or permission changes
+            log_debug "Normalizing: $file (empty diff detected)"
+
+            if [[ "$DRY_RUN" != "true" ]]; then
+                # Normalize line endings
+                if [[ -f "$file" ]]; then
+                    tr -d '\r' < "$file" > "${file}.tmp" 2>/dev/null && mv "${file}.tmp" "$file"
+                    sed -i 's/[[:space:]]*$//' "$file" 2>/dev/null || true
+                    git add "$file" 2>/dev/null || true
+                    fixed_count=$((fixed_count + 1))
+                fi
+            else
+                log_info "[DRY RUN] Would normalize: $file"
+            fi
+        fi
+    done <<< "$changed_files"
+
+    if [[ $fixed_count -gt 0 ]]; then
+        log_info "Fixed $fixed_count file(s) with empty modifications"
+    fi
+}

+# Fix Git extension interference (GitKraken, fsmonitor, fileMode issues)
+# This addresses false "modified" status in VSCode caused by:
+# - GitKraken's gk.exe extension cache (.git/gk/)
+# - core.fsmonitor incompatibility with WSL
+# - core.fileMode tracking permission changes
+fix_git_extension_interference() {
+    log_info "Checking for Git extension interference..."
+
+    local fixed_any=false
+
+    # 1. Remove GitKraken cache directory if present
+    if [[ -d ".git/gk" ]]; then
+        log_warn "Found GitKraken cache directory (.git/gk/), removing..."
+        if [[ "$DRY_RUN" == "true" ]]; then
+            log_info "[DRY RUN] Would remove .git/gk/"
+        else
+            rm -rf .git/gk
+            log_info "Removed GitKraken cache directory"
+            fixed_any=true
+        fi
+    fi
+
+    # 2. Check and disable core.fsmonitor if enabled (incompatible with WSL)
+    local fsmonitor_enabled
+    fsmonitor_enabled=$(git_cmd_capture "git config core.fsmonitor" 2>/dev/null || true)
+    if [[ "$fsmonitor_enabled" == "true" ]]; then
+        log_warn "core.fsmonitor is enabled (incompatible with WSL), disabling..."
+        if [[ "$DRY_RUN" == "true" ]]; then
+            log_info "[DRY RUN] Would disable core.fsmonitor"
+        else
+            git_cmd "git config core.fsmonitor false"
+            log_info "Disabled core.fsmonitor"
+            fixed_any=true
+        fi
+    fi
+
+    # 3. Check and disable core.fileMode if it's causing false modifications
+    # This is common on Windows/WSL where file permissions don't map well
+    local filemode_enabled
+    filemode_enabled=$(git_cmd_capture "git config core.fileMode" 2>/dev/null || true)
+    if [[ "$filemode_enabled" == "true" ]]; then
+        # Check if there are files showing as modified but only permission changes
+        local perm_changes
+        perm_changes=$(git_cmd_capture "git diff --name-only" 2>/dev/null | while IFS= read -r file; do
+            [[ -z "$file" ]] && continue
+            # Check if diff is only mode changes
+            local diff_output
+            diff_output=$(git diff -- "$file" 2>/dev/null || true)
+            if [[ -n "$diff_output" ]] && echo "$diff_output" | grep -q "^old mode\|^new mode" && ! echo "$diff_output" | grep -q "^@@"; then
+                echo "$file"
+            fi
+        done)
+
+        if [[ -n "$perm_changes" ]]; then
+            log_warn "core.fileMode is causing false modifications, disabling..."
+            if [[ "$DRY_RUN" == "true" ]]; then
+                log_info "[DRY RUN] Would disable core.fileMode"
+            else
+                git_cmd "git config core.fileMode false"
+                log_info "Disabled core.fileMode"
+                fixed_any=true
+            fi
+        fi
+    fi
+
+    # 4. If we made any fixes, rebuild the git index to clear stale state
+    if [[ "$fixed_any" == "true" ]] && [[ "$DRY_RUN" != "true" ]]; then
+        log_info "Rebuilding git index after configuration changes..."
+        rm -f .git/index
+        git_cmd "git reset --mixed HEAD" >/dev/null
+        log_info "Git index rebuilt"
+    fi
+
+    return 0
+}

+    if [[ "$LOG_LEVEL" == "DEBUG" ]]; then
+        log_debug "Debug logging enabled"
+    fi
+
+    if [[ "$DRY_RUN" == "true" ]]; then
+        log_info "Dry run mode enabled"
+    fi
+
+    if [[ "$AUTO_MESSAGE" == "false" ]]; then
+        log_info "Auto message generation disabled"
+    fi
+

+    validate_git_config

+# Auto-squash duplicate commits with the same subject
+# Uses git rebase --interactive with auto-squash to merge commits that have identical messages
+auto_squash_duplicates() {
+    local max_commits="${1:-$HISTORY_DEPTH}"
+    log_info "Checking for duplicate commits to squash (last $max_commits)..."
+
+    # Get commit subjects with their hashes
+    local commits
+    commits=$(git log -n "$max_commits" --format='%H %s' 2>/dev/null)
+
+    if [[ -z "$commits" ]]; then
+        log_debug "No commits to analyze"
+        return 0
+    fi
+
+    # Find duplicates by subject
+    declare -A subject_hashes
+    declare -A subject_count
+    local duplicates_found=0
+
+    while IFS= read -r line; do
+        [[ -z "$line" ]] && continue
+        local hash="${line%% *}"
+        local subject="${line#* }"
+        subject_count["$subject"]=$((${subject_count["$subject"]:-0} + 1))
+        if [[ ${subject_count["$subject"]} -eq 2 ]]; then
+            # First duplicate found - record both hashes
+            subject_hashes["$subject"]="${subject_hashes["$subject"]:-} $hash"
+            duplicates_found=$((duplicates_found + 1))
+        elif [[ ${subject_count["$subject"]} -gt 2 ]]; then
+            subject_hashes["$subject"]="${subject_hashes["$subject"]:-} $hash"
+        fi
+    done <<< "$commits"
+
+    if [[ $duplicates_found -eq 0 ]]; then
+        log_info "No duplicate commits found"
+        return 0
+    fi
+
+    log_warn "Found $duplicates_found duplicate commit subject(s)"
+
+    if [[ "$DRY_RUN" == "true" ]]; then
+        for subj in "${!subject_hashes[@]}"; do
+            log_info "[DRY RUN] Would squash duplicates for: $subj"
+        done
+        return 0
+    fi
+
+    # Perform the squash using git rebase --autosquash
+    local current_branch
+    current_branch=$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo "HEAD")
+    if [[ "$current_branch" == "HEAD" ]]; then
+        log_warn "Detached HEAD - skipping auto-squash"
+        return 0
+    fi
+
+    # Create a backup branch before rebase
+    local backup_branch="backup/pre-squash-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
+    git_cmd "git branch \"$backup_branch\"" >/dev/null 2>&1
+    log_info "Created backup branch: $backup_branch"
+
+    # Collect all duplicate commit hashes (all but the first of each group)
+    local squash_hashes=""
+    for subj in "${!subject_hashes[@]}"; do
+        local hashes="${subject_hashes[$subj]}"
+        # Skip the first hash (to keep), collect the rest
+        local rest
+        rest=$(echo "$hashes" | cut -d' ' -f2-)
+        squash_hashes="$squash_hashes $rest"
+    done
+
+    if [[ -z "$squash_hashes" ]]; then
+        log_info "No commits to squash"
+        return 0
+    fi
+
+    log_info "Squashing duplicate commits using git reset --soft + recommit..."
+
+    # Get the first commit subject (to use for the squashed commit)
+    local first_subject
+    first_subject=$(echo "${!subject_hashes[@]}" | head -1)
+    first_subject="${subject_hashes[$first_subject]%% *}"
+    first_subject=$(git log -1 --format='%s' "$first_subject" 2>/dev/null || echo "chore: squashed commits")
+
+    # Strategy: reset to the parent of the first duplicate, then recommit with all changes
+    # Find the earliest commit among duplicates to determine reset point
+    local earliest_hash
+    earliest_hash=$(git rev-parse HEAD~$((max_commits - 1)) 2>/dev/null || git rev-parse HEAD)
+
+    # For each duplicate group, reset to before the first commit and recommit
+    for subj in "${!subject_hashes[@]}"; do
+        local hashes="${subject_hashes[$subj]}"
+        local first_hash
+        first_hash=$(echo "$hashes" | awk '{print $1}')
+        local parent
+        parent=$(git rev-parse "${first_hash}^" 2>/dev/null || echo "")
+
+        if [[ -z "$parent" ]]; then
+            continue
+        fi
+
+        # Reset to parent, keeping all changes from first commit
+        git_cmd "git reset --soft \"$parent\"" >/dev/null 2>&1
+        # Commit with the original message
+        local msg
+        msg=$(git log -1 --format='%s' "$first_hash" 2>/dev/null || echo "chore: squashed")
+        git_cmd "git commit -m \"$msg\"" >/dev/null 2>&1
+        log_debug "Squashed group: $msg"
+    done
+
+    log_info "Auto-squash completed"
+    return 0
+}
+
+# Auto-cleanup orphaned branches (merged but not deleted)
+auto_cleanup_orphaned_branches() {
+    log_info "Checking for orphaned branches to cleanup..."
+
+    local current_branch
+    current_branch=$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo "HEAD")
+
+    if [[ "$current_branch" == "HEAD" ]]; then
+        log_debug "Detached HEAD - skipping orphaned branch cleanup"
+        return 0
+    fi
+
+    # Find merged branches (excluding current, main, master, and remotes)
+    local orphaned
+    orphaned=$(git branch --merged "$current_branch" 2>/dev/null | grep -vE '^\*|^\s*(main|master|HEAD|remotes/.*)$' | sed 's/^[* ]*//' | tr -d ' ')
+
+    if [[ -z "$orphaned" ]]; then
+        log_info "No orphaned branches to cleanup"
+        return 0
+    fi
+
+    log_warn "Found orphaned branches: $orphaned"
+
+    if [[ "$DRY_RUN" == "true" ]]; then
+        for b in $orphaned; do
+            log_info "[DRY RUN] Would delete branch: $b"
+        done
+        return 0
+    fi
+
+    local cleaned=0
+    for b in $orphaned; do
+        if git_cmd "git branch -d \"$b\"" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+            log_info "Deleted merged branch: $b"
+            cleaned=$((cleaned + 1))
+        else
+            log_warn "Could not delete branch: $b (may have unmerged changes)"
+        fi
+    done
+
+    if [[ $cleaned -gt 0 ]]; then
+        log_info "Cleaned up $cleaned orphaned branch(es)"
+    fi
+
+    return 0
+}

+---
+name: generate-slash-command
+description: Generate a new slash command definition (Markdown) and optional executable wrapper script following project best practices. When to use this skill: you need to create a new slash command for the agent to use, ensuring it follows the standard format for documentation, arguments, and execution. Include keywords: slash command, command generation, documentation, wrapper script, automation.
+---
+
+# When to use
+Use this skill when you want to expose a new capability or skill as a slash command. This ensures the command is properly documented and (optionally) has a robust wrapper script for execution.
+
+# When NOT to use
+- Do not use this skill to create the actual logic of the command (the skill or script it invokes). Create those first.
+- Do not use this skill if you only need a simple script without a slash command interface.
+
+# Inputs required
+- `name`: The name of the slash command (e.g., `git-auto-commit`).
+- `description`: A brief description of what the command does.
+- `arguments`: A list of arguments the command accepts (e.g., `<-m "message">`).
+- `usage_examples`: Examples of how to use the command.
+- `features`: Key features of the command.
+- `env_vars`: (Optional) Environment variables used by the command.
+- `exit_codes`: (Optional) Exit codes and their meanings.
+- `generate_wrapper`: (Optional) Boolean, whether to generate a `.sh` wrapper script. Default: `true`.
+- `target_script`: (Optional) Path to the script the wrapper should invoke. Required if `generate_wrapper` is `true`.
+
+# Workflow
+1.  **Gather Inputs**: Ensure all required parameters are provided.
+2.  **Generate Markdown**: Create `.roo/commands/<name>.md` using the standard template.
+3.  **Generate Wrapper (Optional)**: If requested, create `.roo/commands/<name>.sh`.
+4.  **Verify**: Ensure files are created and have correct permissions (if applicable).
+

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# generate-slash-command skill script
+# Generates a slash command Markdown file and optional wrapper script
+
+set -euo pipefail
+
+# Default values
+GENERATE_WRAPPER=true
+TARGET_SCRIPT=""
+ENV_VARS=""
+EXIT_CODES=""
+
+# Parse command line arguments
+while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
+    case $1 in
+        --name)
+            NAME="$2"
+            shift 2
+            ;;
+        --description)
+            DESCRIPTION="$2"
+            shift 2
+            ;;
+        --arguments)
+            ARGUMENTS="$2"
+            shift 2
+            ;;
+        --usage-examples)
+            USAGE_EXAMPLES="$2"
+            shift 2
+            ;;
+        --features)
+            FEATURES="$2"
+            shift 2
+            ;;
+        --env-vars)
+            ENV_VARS="$2"
+            shift 2
+            ;;
+        --exit-codes)
+            EXIT_CODES="$2"
+            shift 2
+            ;;
+        --generate-wrapper)
+            GENERATE_WRAPPER="$2"
+            shift 2
+            ;;
+        --target-script)
+            TARGET_SCRIPT="$2"
+            shift 2
+            ;;
+        *)
+            echo "Unknown argument: $1"
+            exit 1
+            ;;
+    esac
+done
+
+# Validate required arguments
+if [[ -z "${NAME:-}" ]]; then
+    echo "Error: --name is required"
+    exit 1
+fi
+if [[ -z "${DESCRIPTION:-}" ]]; then
+    echo "Error: --description is required"
+    exit 1
+fi
+if [[ -z "${ARGUMENTS:-}" ]]; then
+    echo "Error: --arguments is required"
+    exit 1
+fi
+if [[ -z "${USAGE_EXAMPLES:-}" ]]; then
+    echo "Error: --usage-examples is required"
+    exit 1
+fi
+if [[ -z "${FEATURES:-}" ]]; then
+    echo "Error: --features is required"
+    exit 1
+fi

+# Git Auto Commit - Changes and Fixes
+
+## Summary
+
+This document describes the fixes and enhancements made to the `git-auto-commit` skill to address the error shown in the image and improve robustness.
+
+## Root Cause Analysis
+
+The image showed a VSCode Git panel with files showing `+0 -0 M` (modified) status but `0 of 8 staged` - indicating changes were not being properly staged. The root causes identified:
+
+1. **Broken `check_secrets()` function**: The function had an early `return 0` statement that made it a no-op, causing it to always pass without actually checking for secrets
+2. **No authentication failure detection**: Git operations would fail silently without clear error messages when credentials were invalid or expired
+3. **No network error handling**: Network failures during push/fetch operations were not retried
+4. **Poor merge conflict recovery**: The sync process didn't properly handle rebase conflicts
+5. **Line ending normalization issues**: The `normalize_staged_files()` function used `sed -i` which could fail on certain file types
+
+## Changes Made
+
+### 1. Fixed `check_secrets()` Function (git-utils.sh)
+
+**Before**: The function had a `return 0` before the actual secret checking logic, making it always pass.
+
+**After**:
+- Removed the premature return
+- Added proper secret pattern matching using grep with comprehensive patterns
+- Patterns now cover: API keys, tokens, passwords, private keys, connection strings
+- Returns exit code 4 when secrets are detected
+
+### 2. Added Authentication Failure Detection (git-utils.sh)
+
+New functions added:
+- `is_auth_failure()`: Detects authentication errors from git output
+- `classify_git_error()`: Classifies errors as auth, network, conflict, permission, or unknown
+
+Authentication failure patterns detected:
+- `Authentication failed`
+- `Could not read Password`
+- `Permission denied` (for push operations)
+- `Access denied`
+- SSH key/identity issues
+
+### 3. Added Network Error Handling with Retry Logic (git-utils.sh)
+
+Enhanced `git_cmd()` and `git_cmd_capture()` functions with:
+- Configurable retry count (3 for git_cmd, 2 for git_cmd_capture)
+- Automatic retry on network errors with exponential backoff
+- Clear error messages for network failures
+
+New function:
+- `is_network_error()`: Detects network-related errors (connection refused, timed out, reset, DNS failures, SSL/TLS errors)
+
+### 4. Improved Merge Conflict Recovery (git-utils.sh)
+
+New function:
+- `recover_merge_conflicts()`: Detects and attempts to recover from merge conflicts
+  - Checks for active rebase/merge state
+  - Aborts conflicted operations
+  - Identifies conflicted files
+  - Returns appropriate exit codes
+
+Enhanced `sync_repository_state()`:
+- Better conflict detection during pull --rebase
+- Automatic abort and stash restoration on conflict
+- More detailed error logging
+
+### 5. Fixed Line Ending Normalization (git-auto-commit.sh)
+
+**Before**: Used `sed -i 's/\r$//'` which could fail on certain files
+
+**After**:
+- Uses `tr -d '\r'` for more reliable CRLF removal
+- Added dry-run support
+- Re-stages normalized files to ensure changes are captured
+- Added debug logging
+
+### 6. Added Safe Push Function (git-utils.sh)
+
+New function:
+- `safe_push()`: Robust push with retry logic
+  - Retries up to 3 times on network errors
+  - Detects authentication failures and provides clear messages
+  - Handles non-fast-forward errors by attempting to sync
+  - Provides detailed error output
+
+### 7. Added Git Configuration Validation (git-utils.sh)
+
+New function:
+- `validate_git_config()`: Validates git setup before operations
+  - Checks user.name and user.email are set
+  - Tests remote connectivity with lightweight ls-remote
+  - Provides warnings for missing configuration
+
+### 8. Enhanced Main Script (git-auto-commit.sh)
+
+Updated the main execution flow:
+- Uses `safe_push()` instead of direct `git push`
+- Attempts conflict recovery if push fails
+- Better error handling with appropriate exit codes
+- Improved logging throughout
+
+## Testing
+
+All self-tests pass successfully:
+```
+[INFO] Test 1: No changes scenario - PASSED
+[INFO] Test 2: Simple changes scenario - PASSED
+[INFO] Test 3: Dry run scenario - PASSED
+```
+
+## Exit Codes
+
+The script now provides more specific exit codes:
+- `0` - Success or no changes (idempotent)
+- `1` - General error
+- `2` - Git error (repository issues, configuration)
+- `3` - Push error (after all retries exhausted)
+- `4` - Validation error (secrets found, config issues)
+- `5` - Conflict detected (manual resolution required)
+
+## Edge Cases Handled
+
+1. **Authentication failures**: Clear error messages with troubleshooting guidance
+2. **Network errors**: Automatic retry with backoff
+3. **Merge conflicts**: Detection, abort, and stash restoration
+4. **No changes**: Idempotent exit (exit 0)
+5. **Detached HEAD**: Warning but continues
+6. **Missing git config**: Warning but continues
+7. **Remote unreachable**: Graceful degradation with clear error messages
+8. **Staged file normalization**: Safe handling of line endings and whitespace
+
+## Files Modified
+
+1. `.roo/skills/git-auto-commit/scripts/lib/git-utils.sh`
+   - Fixed `check_secrets()` function
+   - Added `is_auth_failure()`, `is_network_error()`, `is_merge_conflict()`, `classify_git_error()`
+   - Enhanced `git_cmd()` and `git_cmd_capture()` with retry logic
+   - Enhanced `sync_repository_state()` with better error handling
+   - Added `safe_push()` function
+   - Added `recover_merge_conflicts()` function
+   - Added `validate_git_config()` function
+   - Added `init_skill()` integration with config validation
+
+2. `.roo/skills/git-auto-commit/scripts/git-auto-commit.sh`
+   - Fixed `normalize_staged_files()` function
+   - Updated main execution to use `safe_push()`
+   - Added conflict recovery attempt after push failure
+   - Improved error handling and logging

 # Initialize skill
 init_skill
+normalize_staged_files() {
+    log_debug "Normalizing line endings and whitespace in staged files..."
+
+    git diff --cached --name-only -z | while IFS= read -r -d '' file; do
+        if [[ -f "$file" ]]; then
+            # Remove carriage returns and trailing whitespace
+            if [[ "$DRY_RUN" == "true" ]]; then
+                log_debug "[DRY RUN] Would normalize: $file"
+            else
+                # Use tr for CRLF removal and sed for trailing whitespace
+                tr -d '\r' < "$file" > "${file}.tmp" && mv "${file}.tmp" "$file"
+                sed -i 's/[[:space:]]*$//' "$file"
+                # Re-stage the normalized file
+                git_cmd "git add \"$file\"" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
+            fi
+        fi
+    done
+}

+# Classify git errors for appropriate handling
+# Returns: auth, network, conflict, permission, or unknown
+classify_git_error() {
+    local output="$1"
+
+    if is_auth_failure "$output"; then
+        echo "auth"
+        return
+    fi
+
+    if is_network_error "$output"; then
+        echo "network"
+        return
+    fi
+
+    if is_merge_conflict "$output"; then
+        echo "conflict"
+        return
+    fi
+
+    if echo "$output" | grep -qE "(permission denied|fatal: .*: Permission denied)"; then
+        echo "permission"
+        return
+    fi
+
+    echo "unknown"
+}
+
+# Check if error is authentication related
+is_auth_failure() {
+    local output="$1"
+    echo "$output" | grep -iE "(fatal: .*: Authentication failed|fatal: .*: Could not read Password|fatal: .*: unable to access|fatal: .*: Permission denied.*push|fatal: .*: Access denied|fatal: .*: Bad owner or permissions on .*\.ssh/config|fatal: .*: no such identity)" | grep -v "Permission denied to .*\.ssh/config" | head -1
+}
+
+# Check if error is network related
+is_network_error() {
+    local output="$1"
+    echo "$output" | grep -iE "(Connection refused|Connection timed out|Connection reset|Connection aborted|Could not resolve host|Network is unreachable|SSL_ERROR|TLS handshake failed|fatal: .*: unable to access.*Connection)" | head -1
+}
+
+# Check if error is a merge conflict
+is_merge_conflict() {
+    local output="$1"
+    echo "$output" | grep -iE "(CONFLICT|Automatic merge failed|merge conflict)" | head -1
+}

+# Safe push with retry and conflict recovery
+safe_push() {
+    local push_cmd="$1"
+    local max_retries=3
+    local retry_count=0
+    local exit_code=0
+
+    log_info "Pushing with retry logic (max $max_retries attempts)..."
+
+    while [[ $retry_count -lt $max_retries ]]; do
+        if [[ "$DRY_RUN" == "true" ]]; then
+            log_info "[DRY RUN] Would run: $push_cmd"
+            return 0
+        fi
+
+        local push_output
+        push_output=$(eval "$push_cmd" 2>&1)
+        exit_code=$?
+
+        if [[ $exit_code -eq 0 ]]; then
+            log_info "Push successful on attempt $((retry_count + 1))"
+            return 0
+        fi
+
+        log_warn "Push attempt $((retry_count + 1)) failed (exit code: $exit_code)"
+
+        # Check error type
+        if is_auth_failure "$push_output"; then
+            log_error "AUTHENTICATION FAILURE during push"
+            log_error "Please check your git credentials"
+            return 3
+        fi
+
+        if is_network_error "$push_output"; then
+            retry_count=$((retry_count + 1))
+            if [[ $retry_count -lt $max_retries ]]; then
+                log_warn "Network error, retrying in 3 seconds..."
+                sleep 3
+                continue
+            fi
+        fi
+
+        if echo "$push_output" | grep -qE "(non-fast-forward|rejected|fetch first)"; then
+            log_warn "Push rejected - remote has changes, attempting to sync..."
+            if git_cmd "git fetch origin" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+                if git_cmd "git rebase origin/HEAD" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+                    log_info "Repository synced, retrying push..."
+                    retry_count=$((retry_count + 1))
+                    sleep 1
+                    continue
+                fi
+            fi
+        fi
+
+        # For other errors, don't retry
+        break
+    done
+
+    log_error "Push failed after $max_retries attempts"
+    log_error "Push output: $push_output"
+    return 3
+}
+
+# Recover from merge conflicts
+recover_merge_conflicts() {
+    log_info "Attempting to recover from merge conflicts..."
+
+    # Check if we're in a merge state
+    if [[ -d .git/rebase-merge ]] || [[ -d .git/rebase-apply ]]; then
+        log_warn "Active rebase/merge operation detected"
+        if [[ "$DRY_RUN" == "true" ]]; then
+            log_info "[DRY RUN] Would abort current merge/rebase"
+            return 0
+        fi
+        # Abort the operation and try again
+        git_cmd "git rebase --abort" >/dev/null 2>&1 || git_cmd "git merge --abort" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
+    fi
+
+    # Check for conflict markers in files
+    local conflict_files
+    conflict_files=$(git_cmd_capture "git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U" 2>/dev/null || true)
+
+    if [[ -n "$conflict_files" ]]; then
+        log_warn "Conflicted files: $conflict_files"
+        log_error "Automatic conflict resolution not possible - manual intervention required"
+        return 5
+    fi
+
+    log_info "No merge conflicts detected"
+    return 0
+}
+
+# Validate git configuration
+validate_git_config() {
+    log_info "Validating git configuration..."
+
+    local user_name user_email
+    user_name=$(git_cmd_capture "git config user.name" 2>/dev/null || true)
+    user_email=$(git_cmd_capture "git config user.email" 2>/dev/null || true)
+
+    if [[ -z "$user_name" ]]; then
+        log_warn "Git user.name not set - commits may fail"
+    fi
+
+    if [[ -z "$user_email" ]]; then
+        log_warn "Git user.email not set - commits may fail"
+    fi
+
+    # Check remote connectivity
+    local remote_url
+    remote_url=$(git_cmd_capture "git config --get remote.origin.url" 2>/dev/null || true)
+
+    if [[ -n "$remote_url" ]]; then
+        log_debug "Remote URL: $remote_url"
+        # Test connectivity with a lightweight operation
+        if ! git_cmd_capture "git ls-remote --heads origin HEAD" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+            log_warn "Cannot reach remote - check network and credentials"
+            return 2
+        fi
+    fi
+
+    log_info "Git configuration validated"
+    return 0
+}
