+sync_repository_state() {
+    local branch="$1"
+    log_info "Syncing repository state for branch '$branch'..."
+    
+    # Check for uncommitted changes
+    local has_changes
+    if ! git_cmd_capture "git diff-index --quiet HEAD --"; then
+        has_changes=true
+        log_info "Uncommitted changes detected, stashing..."
+        if [[ "$DRY_RUN" == "true" ]]; then
+            log_info "[DRY RUN] Would run: git stash push -u -m \"auto-commit stash before sync\""
+        else
+            # Stash changes including untracked files
+            if ! git_cmd "git stash push -u -m \"auto-commit stash before sync\""; then
+                log_error "Failed to stash changes"
+                return 2
+            fi
+        fi

+        has_changes=false
+        log_info "No uncommitted changes found"
+    fi
+

+    git_cmd "git fetch origin" >/dev/null
+

+    local local_hash
+    local remote_hash
+    local_hash=$(git_cmd "git rev-parse $branch")
+    remote_hash=$(git_cmd "git rev-parse origin/$branch")
+    
+    if [[ "$local_hash" != "$remote_hash" ]]; then
+        log_info "Branch is behind origin, performing pull --rebase..."
+        if [[ "$DRY_RUN" == "true" ]]; then
+            log_info "[DRY RUN] Would run: git pull --rebase origin $branch"
+        else
+            if ! git_cmd "git pull --rebase origin $branch"; then
+                log_error "Failed to pull --rebase"
+                # If we stashed changes, try to restore them before returning
+                if [[ "$has_changes" == "true" && "$DRY_RUN" != "true" ]]; then
+                    log_warn "Attempting to restore stashed changes after pull failure..."
+                    git_cmd "git stash pop" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
+                fi
+                return 5
+            fi
+        fi
+    else
+        log_info "Branch is up to date with origin"
+    fi
+    
+    # Pop stash if we had changes
+    if [[ "$has_changes" == "true" ]]; then
+        log_info "Restoring stashed changes..."
+        if [[ "$DRY_RUN" == "true" ]]; then
+            log_info "[DRY RUN] Would run: git stash pop"
+        else
+            if ! git_cmd "git stash pop"; then
+                log_warn "Conflicts occurred when popping stash - manual resolution may be needed"
+                # Don't return error here as the pull succeeded, just warn about conflicts
+            else
+                log_info "Stashed changes restored successfully"
+            fi
+        fi
+    fi
+    
+    log_info "Repository state synchronized"

+# Initialize skill
+init_skill() {
+    log_debug "Initializing git-auto-commit skill"
+
+    # Set up logging based on environment
+    if [[ "$LOG_LEVEL" == "DEBUG" ]]; then
+        log_debug "Debug logging enabled"
+    fi
+
+    if [[ "$DRY_RUN" == "true" ]]; then
+        log_info "Dry run mode enabled"
+    fi
+
+    if [[ "$AUTO_MESSAGE" == "false" ]]; then
+        log_info "Auto message generation disabled"
+    fi
+
+    # Validate git configuration
+    validate_git_config
+}
+
+# Auto-squash duplicate commits with the same subject
+# Uses git rebase --interactive with auto-squash to merge commits that have identical messages
+auto_squash_duplicates() {
+    local max_commits="${1:-$HISTORY_DEPTH}"
+    log_info "Checking for duplicate commits to squash (last $max_commits)..."
+
+    # Get commit subjects with their hashes
+    local commits
+    commits=$(git log -n "$max_commits" --format='%H %s' 2>/dev/null)
+
+    if [[ -z "$commits" ]]; then
+        log_debug "No commits to analyze"
+        return 0
+    fi
+
+    # Find duplicates by subject
+    declare -A subject_hashes
+    declare -A subject_count
+    local duplicates_found=0
+
+    while IFS= read -r line; do
+        [[ -z "$line" ]] && continue
+        local hash="${line%% *}"
+        local subject="${line#* }"
+        subject_count["$subject"]=$((${subject_count["$subject"]:-0} + 1))
+        if [[ ${subject_count["$subject"]} -eq 2 ]]; then
+            # First duplicate found - record both hashes
+            subject_hashes["$subject"]="${subject_hashes["$subject"]:-} $hash"
+            duplicates_found=$((duplicates_found + 1))
+        elif [[ ${subject_count["$subject"]} -gt 2 ]]; then
+            subject_hashes["$subject"]="${subject_hashes["$subject"]:-} $hash"
+        fi
+    done <<< "$commits"
+
+    if [[ $duplicates_found -eq 0 ]]; then
+        log_info "No duplicate commits found"
+        return 0
+    fi
+
+    log_warn "Found $duplicates_found duplicate commit subject(s)"
+
+    if [[ "$DRY_RUN" == "true" ]]; then
+        for subj in "${!subject_hashes[@]}"; do
+            log_info "[DRY RUN] Would squash duplicates for: $subj"
+        done
+        return 0
+    fi
+
+    # Perform the squash using git rebase --autosquash
+    local current_branch
+    current_branch=$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo "HEAD")
+    if [[ "$current_branch" == "HEAD" ]]; then
+        log_warn "Detached HEAD - skipping auto-squash"
+        return 0
+    fi
+
+    # Create a backup branch before rebase
+    local backup_branch="backup/pre-squash-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
+    git_cmd "git branch \"$backup_branch\"" >/dev/null 2>&1
+    log_info "Created backup branch: $backup_branch"
+
+    # Collect all duplicate commit hashes (all but the first of each group)
+    local squash_hashes=""
+    for subj in "${!subject_hashes[@]}"; do
+        local hashes="${subject_hashes[$subj]}"
+        # Skip the first hash (to keep), collect the rest
+        local rest
+        rest=$(echo "$hashes" | cut -d' ' -f2-)
+        squash_hashes="$squash_hashes $rest"
+    done
+
+    if [[ -z "$squash_hashes" ]]; then
+        log_info "No commits to squash"
+        return 0
+    fi
+
+    log_info "Squashing duplicate commits using git reset --soft + recommit..."
+
+    # Get the first commit subject (to use for the squashed commit)
+    local first_subject
+    first_subject=$(echo "${!subject_hashes[@]}" | head -1)
+    first_subject="${subject_hashes[$first_subject]%% *}"
+    first_subject=$(git log -1 --format='%s' "$first_subject" 2>/dev/null || echo "chore: squashed commits")
+
+    # Strategy: reset to the parent of the first duplicate, then recommit with all changes
+    # Find the earliest commit among duplicates to determine reset point
+    local earliest_hash
+    earliest_hash=$(git rev-parse HEAD~$((max_commits - 1)) 2>/dev/null || git rev-parse HEAD)
+
+    # For each duplicate group, reset to before the first commit and recommit
+    for subj in "${!subject_hashes[@]}"; do
+        local hashes="${subject_hashes[$subj]}"
+        local first_hash
+        first_hash=$(echo "$hashes" | awk '{print $1}')
+        local parent
+        parent=$(git rev-parse "${first_hash}^" 2>/dev/null || echo "")
+
+        if [[ -z "$parent" ]]; then
+            continue
+        fi
+
+        # Reset to parent, keeping all changes from first commit
+        git_cmd "git reset --soft \"$parent\"" >/dev/null 2>&1
+        # Commit with the original message
+        local msg
+        msg=$(git log -1 --format='%s' "$first_hash" 2>/dev/null || echo "chore: squashed")
+        git_cmd "git commit -m \"$msg\"" >/dev/null 2>&1
+        log_debug "Squashed group: $msg"
+    done
+
+    log_info "Auto-squash completed"
+    return 0
+}
+
+# Auto-cleanup orphaned branches (merged but not deleted)
+auto_cleanup_orphaned_branches() {
+    log_info "Checking for orphaned branches to cleanup..."
+
+    local current_branch
+    current_branch=$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo "HEAD")
+
+    if [[ "$current_branch" == "HEAD" ]]; then
+        log_debug "Detached HEAD - skipping orphaned branch cleanup"
+        return 0
+    fi
+
+    # Find merged branches (excluding current, main, master, and remotes)
+    local orphaned
+    orphaned=$(git branch --merged "$current_branch" 2>/dev/null | grep -vE '^\*|^\s*(main|master|HEAD|remotes/.*)$' | sed 's/^[* ]*//' | tr -d ' ')
+
+    if [[ -z "$orphaned" ]]; then
+        log_info "No orphaned branches to cleanup"
+        return 0
+    fi
+
+    log_warn "Found orphaned branches: $orphaned"
+
+    if [[ "$DRY_RUN" == "true" ]]; then
+        for b in $orphaned; do
+            log_info "[DRY RUN] Would delete branch: $b"
+        done
+        return 0
+    fi
+
+    local cleaned=0
+    for b in $orphaned; do
+        if git_cmd "git branch -d \"$b\"" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+            log_info "Deleted merged branch: $b"
+            cleaned=$((cleaned + 1))
+        else
+            log_warn "Could not delete branch: $b (may have unmerged changes)"
+        fi
+    done
+
+    if [[ $cleaned -gt 0 ]]; then
+        log_info "Cleaned up $cleaned orphaned branch(es)"
+    fi
+
+    return 0
+}

+# Fix Git extension interference (GitKraken, fsmonitor, fileMode issues)
+# This addresses false "modified" status in VSCode caused by:
+# - GitKraken's gk.exe extension cache (.git/gk/)
+# - core.fsmonitor incompatibility with WSL
+# - core.fileMode tracking permission changes
+fix_git_extension_interference() {
+    log_info "Checking for Git extension interference..."
+
+    local fixed_any=false
+
+    # 1. Remove GitKraken cache directory if present
+    if [[ -d ".git/gk" ]]; then
+        log_warn "Found GitKraken cache directory (.git/gk/), removing..."
+        if [[ "$DRY_RUN" == "true" ]]; then
+            log_info "[DRY RUN] Would remove .git/gk/"
+        else
+            rm -rf .git/gk
+            log_info "Removed GitKraken cache directory"
+            fixed_any=true
+        fi
+    fi
+
+    # 2. Check and disable core.fsmonitor if enabled (incompatible with WSL)
+    local fsmonitor_enabled
+    fsmonitor_enabled=$(git_cmd_capture "git config core.fsmonitor" 2>/dev/null || true)
+    if [[ "$fsmonitor_enabled" == "true" ]]; then
+        log_warn "core.fsmonitor is enabled (incompatible with WSL), disabling..."
+        if [[ "$DRY_RUN" == "true" ]]; then
+            log_info "[DRY RUN] Would disable core.fsmonitor"
+        else
+            git_cmd "git config core.fsmonitor false"
+            log_info "Disabled core.fsmonitor"
+            fixed_any=true
+        fi
+    fi
+
+    # 3. Check and disable core.fileMode if it's causing false modifications
+    # This is common on Windows/WSL where file permissions don't map well
+    local filemode_enabled
+    filemode_enabled=$(git_cmd_capture "git config core.fileMode" 2>/dev/null || true)
+    if [[ "$filemode_enabled" == "true" ]]; then
+        # Check if there are files showing as modified but only permission changes
+        local perm_changes
+        perm_changes=$(git_cmd_capture "git diff --name-only" 2>/dev/null | while IFS= read -r file; do
+            [[ -z "$file" ]] && continue
+            # Check if diff is only mode changes
+            local diff_output
+            diff_output=$(git diff -- "$file" 2>/dev/null || true)
+            if [[ -n "$diff_output" ]] && echo "$diff_output" | grep -q "^old mode\|^new mode" && ! echo "$diff_output" | grep -q "^@@"; then
+                echo "$file"
+            fi
+        done)
+
+        if [[ -n "$perm_changes" ]]; then
+            log_warn "core.fileMode is causing false modifications, disabling..."
+            if [[ "$DRY_RUN" == "true" ]]; then
+                log_info "[DRY RUN] Would disable core.fileMode"
+            else
+                git_cmd "git config core.fileMode false"
+                log_info "Disabled core.fileMode"
+                fixed_any=true
+            fi
+        fi
+    fi
+
+    # 4. If we made any fixes, rebuild the git index to clear stale state
+    if [[ "$fixed_any" == "true" ]] && [[ "$DRY_RUN" != "true" ]]; then
+        log_info "Rebuilding git index after configuration changes..."
+        rm -f .git/index
+        git_cmd "git reset --mixed HEAD" >/dev/null
+        log_info "Git index rebuilt"
+    fi
+
+    return 0
+}

+# Git Auto Commit - Changes and Fixes
+
+## Summary
+
+This document describes the fixes and enhancements made to the `git-auto-commit` skill to address the error shown in the image and improve robustness.
+
+## Root Cause Analysis
+
+The image showed a VSCode Git panel with files showing `+0 -0 M` (modified) status but `0 of 8 staged` - indicating changes were not being properly staged. The root causes identified:
+
+1. **Broken `check_secrets()` function**: The function had an early `return 0` statement that made it a no-op, causing it to always pass without actually checking for secrets
+2. **No authentication failure detection**: Git operations would fail silently without clear error messages when credentials were invalid or expired
+3. **No network error handling**: Network failures during push/fetch operations were not retried
+4. **Poor merge conflict recovery**: The sync process didn't properly handle rebase conflicts
+5. **Line ending normalization issues**: The `normalize_staged_files()` function used `sed -i` which could fail on certain file types
+
+## Changes Made
+
+### 1. Fixed `check_secrets()` Function (git-utils.sh)
+
+**Before**: The function had a `return 0` before the actual secret checking logic, making it always pass.
+
+**After**:
+- Removed the premature return
+- Added proper secret pattern matching using grep with comprehensive patterns
+- Patterns now cover: API keys, tokens, passwords, private keys, connection strings
+- Returns exit code 4 when secrets are detected
+
+### 2. Added Authentication Failure Detection (git-utils.sh)
+
+New functions added:
+- `is_auth_failure()`: Detects authentication errors from git output
+- `classify_git_error()`: Classifies errors as auth, network, conflict, permission, or unknown
+
+Authentication failure patterns detected:
+- `Authentication failed`
+- `Could not read Password`
+- `Permission denied` (for push operations)
+- `Access denied`
+- SSH key/identity issues
+
+### 3. Added Network Error Handling with Retry Logic (git-utils.sh)
+
+Enhanced `git_cmd()` and `git_cmd_capture()` functions with:
+- Configurable retry count (3 for git_cmd, 2 for git_cmd_capture)
+- Automatic retry on network errors with exponential backoff
+- Clear error messages for network failures
+
+New function:
+- `is_network_error()`: Detects network-related errors (connection refused, timed out, reset, DNS failures, SSL/TLS errors)
+
+### 4. Improved Merge Conflict Recovery (git-utils.sh)
+
+New function:
+- `recover_merge_conflicts()`: Detects and attempts to recover from merge conflicts
+  - Checks for active rebase/merge state
+  - Aborts conflicted operations
+  - Identifies conflicted files
+  - Returns appropriate exit codes
+
+Enhanced `sync_repository_state()`:
+- Better conflict detection during pull --rebase
+- Automatic abort and stash restoration on conflict
+- More detailed error logging
+
+### 5. Fixed Line Ending Normalization (git-auto-commit.sh)
+
+**Before**: Used `sed -i 's/\r$//'` which could fail on certain files
+
+**After**:
+- Uses `tr -d '\r'` for more reliable CRLF removal
+- Added dry-run support
+- Re-stages normalized files to ensure changes are captured
+- Added debug logging
+
+### 6. Added Safe Push Function (git-utils.sh)
+
+New function:
+- `safe_push()`: Robust push with retry logic
+  - Retries up to 3 times on network errors
+  - Detects authentication failures and provides clear messages
+  - Handles non-fast-forward errors by attempting to sync
+  - Provides detailed error output
+
+### 7. Added Git Configuration Validation (git-utils.sh)
+
+New function:
+- `validate_git_config()`: Validates git setup before operations
+  - Checks user.name and user.email are set
+  - Tests remote connectivity with lightweight ls-remote
+  - Provides warnings for missing configuration
+
+### 8. Enhanced Main Script (git-auto-commit.sh)
+
+Updated the main execution flow:
+- Uses `safe_push()` instead of direct `git push`
+- Attempts conflict recovery if push fails
+- Better error handling with appropriate exit codes
+- Improved logging throughout
+
+## Testing
+
+All self-tests pass successfully:
+```
+[INFO] Test 1: No changes scenario - PASSED
+[INFO] Test 2: Simple changes scenario - PASSED
+[INFO] Test 3: Dry run scenario - PASSED
+```
+
+## Exit Codes
+
+The script now provides more specific exit codes:
+- `0` - Success or no changes (idempotent)
+- `1` - General error
+- `2` - Git error (repository issues, configuration)
+- `3` - Push error (after all retries exhausted)
+- `4` - Validation error (secrets found, config issues)
+- `5` - Conflict detected (manual resolution required)
+
+## Edge Cases Handled
+
+1. **Authentication failures**: Clear error messages with troubleshooting guidance
+2. **Network errors**: Automatic retry with backoff
+3. **Merge conflicts**: Detection, abort, and stash restoration
+4. **No changes**: Idempotent exit (exit 0)
+5. **Detached HEAD**: Warning but continues

+# Classify git errors for appropriate handling
+# Returns: auth, network, conflict, permission, or unknown
+classify_git_error() {
+    local output="$1"
+
+    if is_auth_failure "$output"; then
+        echo "auth"
+        return
+    fi
+
+    if is_network_error "$output"; then
+        echo "network"
+        return
+    fi
+
+    if is_merge_conflict "$output"; then
+        echo "conflict"
+        return
+    fi
+
+    if echo "$output" | grep -qE "(permission denied|fatal: .*: Permission denied)"; then
+        echo "permission"
+        return
+    fi
+
+    echo "unknown"
+}
+
+# Check if error is authentication related
+is_auth_failure() {
+    local output="$1"
+    echo "$output" | grep -iE "(fatal: .*: Authentication failed|fatal: .*: Could not read Password|fatal: .*: unable to access|fatal: .*: Permission denied.*push|fatal: .*: Access denied|fatal: .*: Bad owner or permissions on .*\.ssh/config|fatal: .*: no such identity)" | grep -v "Permission denied to .*\.ssh/config" | head -1
+}
+
+# Check if error is network related
+is_network_error() {
+    local output="$1"
+    echo "$output" | grep -iE "(Connection refused|Connection timed out|Connection reset|Connection aborted|Could not resolve host|Network is unreachable|SSL_ERROR|TLS handshake failed|fatal: .*: unable to access.*Connection)" | head -1
+}
+
+# Check if error is a merge conflict
+is_merge_conflict() {
+    local output="$1"
+    echo "$output" | grep -iE "(CONFLICT|Automatic merge failed|merge conflict)" | head -1
+}

+# Safe push with retry and conflict recovery
+safe_push() {
+    local push_cmd="$1"
+    local max_retries=3
+    local retry_count=0
+    local exit_code=0
+
+    log_info "Pushing with retry logic (max $max_retries attempts)..."
+
+    while [[ $retry_count -lt $max_retries ]]; do
+        if [[ "$DRY_RUN" == "true" ]]; then
+            log_info "[DRY RUN] Would run: $push_cmd"
+            return 0
+        fi
+
+        local push_output
+        push_output=$(eval "$push_cmd" 2>&1)
+        exit_code=$?
+
+        if [[ $exit_code -eq 0 ]]; then
+            log_info "Push successful on attempt $((retry_count + 1))"
+            return 0
+        fi
+
+        log_warn "Push attempt $((retry_count + 1)) failed (exit code: $exit_code)"
+
+        # Check error type
+        if is_auth_failure "$push_output"; then
+            log_error "AUTHENTICATION FAILURE during push"
+            log_error "Please check your git credentials"
+            return 3
+        fi
+
+        if is_network_error "$push_output"; then
+            retry_count=$((retry_count + 1))
+            if [[ $retry_count -lt $max_retries ]]; then
+                log_warn "Network error, retrying in 3 seconds..."
+                sleep 3
+                continue
+            fi
+        fi
+
+        if echo "$push_output" | grep -qE "(non-fast-forward|rejected|fetch first)"; then
+            log_warn "Push rejected - remote has changes, attempting to sync..."
+            if git_cmd "git fetch origin" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+                if git_cmd "git rebase origin/HEAD" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+                    log_info "Repository synced, retrying push..."
+                    retry_count=$((retry_count + 1))
+                    sleep 1
+                    continue
+                fi
+            fi
+        fi
+
+        # For other errors, don't retry
+        break
+    done
+
+    log_error "Push failed after $max_retries attempts"
+    log_error "Push output: $push_output"
+    return 3
+}
+
+# Recover from merge conflicts
+recover_merge_conflicts() {
+    log_info "Attempting to recover from merge conflicts..."
+
+    # Check if we're in a merge state
+    if [[ -d .git/rebase-merge ]] || [[ -d .git/rebase-apply ]]; then
+        log_warn "Active rebase/merge operation detected"
+        if [[ "$DRY_RUN" == "true" ]]; then
+            log_info "[DRY RUN] Would abort current merge/rebase"
+            return 0
+        fi
+        # Abort the operation and try again
+        git_cmd "git rebase --abort" >/dev/null 2>&1 || git_cmd "git merge --abort" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
+    fi
+
+    # Check for conflict markers in files
+    local conflict_files
+    conflict_files=$(git_cmd_capture "git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U" 2>/dev/null || true)
+
+    if [[ -n "$conflict_files" ]]; then
+        log_warn "Conflicted files: $conflict_files"
+        log_error "Automatic conflict resolution not possible - manual intervention required"
+        return 5
+    fi
+
+    log_info "No merge conflicts detected"
+    return 0
+}
+
+# Validate git configuration
+validate_git_config() {
+    log_info "Validating git configuration..."
+
+    local user_name user_email
+    user_name=$(git_cmd_capture "git config user.name" 2>/dev/null || true)
+    user_email=$(git_cmd_capture "git config user.email" 2>/dev/null || true)
+
+    if [[ -z "$user_name" ]]; then
+        log_warn "Git user.name not set - commits may fail"
+    fi
+
+    if [[ -z "$user_email" ]]; then
+        log_warn "Git user.email not set - commits may fail"
+    fi
+
+    # Check remote connectivity
+    local remote_url
+    remote_url=$(git_cmd_capture "git config --get remote.origin.url" 2>/dev/null || true)
+
+    if [[ -n "$remote_url" ]]; then
+        log_debug "Remote URL: $remote_url"
+        # Test connectivity with a lightweight operation
+        if ! git_cmd_capture "git ls-remote --heads origin HEAD" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+            log_warn "Cannot reach remote - check network and credentials"
+            return 2
+        fi
+    fi
+
+    log_info "Git configuration validated"
+    return 0
+}

+---
+name: generate-slash-command
+description: Generate a new slash command definition (Markdown) and optional executable wrapper script following project best practices. When to use this skill: you need to create a new slash command for the agent to use, ensuring it follows the standard format for documentation, arguments, and execution. Include keywords: slash command, command generation, documentation, wrapper script, automation.
+---
+
+# When to use
+Use this skill when you want to expose a new capability or skill as a slash command. This ensures the command is properly documented and (optionally) has a robust wrapper script for execution.
+
+# When NOT to use
+- Do not use this skill to create the actual logic of the command (the skill or script it invokes). Create those first.
+- Do not use this skill if you only need a simple script without a slash command interface.
+
+# Inputs required
+- `name`: The name of the slash command (e.g., `git-auto-commit`).
+- `description`: A brief description of what the command does.
+- `arguments`: A list of arguments the command accepts (e.g., `<-m "message">`).
+- `usage_examples`: Examples of how to use the command.
+- `features`: Key features of the command.
+- `env_vars`: (Optional) Environment variables used by the command.
+- `exit_codes`: (Optional) Exit codes and their meanings.
+- `generate_wrapper`: (Optional) Boolean, whether to generate a `.sh` wrapper script. Default: `true`.
+- `target_script`: (Optional) Path to the script the wrapper should invoke. Required if `generate_wrapper` is `true`.
+
+# Workflow
+1.  **Gather Inputs**: Ensure all required parameters are provided.
+2.  **Generate Markdown**: Create `.roo/commands/<name>.md` using the standard template.
+3.  **Generate Wrapper (Optional)**: If requested, create `.roo/commands/<name>.sh`.
+4.  **Verify**: Ensure files are created and have correct permissions (if applicable).
+
+# Files
+- [`.roo/skills/generate-slash-command/assets/command-template.md`](assets/command-template.md): Template for the slash command Markdown file.
+- [`.roo/skills/generate-slash-command/assets/wrapper-template.sh`](assets/wrapper-template.sh): Template for the executable wrapper script.

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# generate-slash-command skill script
+# Generates a slash command Markdown file and optional wrapper script
+
+set -euo pipefail
+
+# Default values
+GENERATE_WRAPPER=true
+TARGET_SCRIPT=""
+ENV_VARS=""
+EXIT_CODES=""
+
+# Parse command line arguments
+while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
+    case $1 in
+        --name)
+            NAME="$2"
+            shift 2
+            ;;
+        --description)
+            DESCRIPTION="$2"
+            shift 2
+            ;;
+        --arguments)
+            ARGUMENTS="$2"
+            shift 2
+            ;;
+        --usage-examples)
+            USAGE_EXAMPLES="$2"
+            shift 2
+            ;;
+        --features)
+            FEATURES="$2"
+            shift 2
+            ;;
+        --env-vars)
+            ENV_VARS="$2"
+            shift 2
+            ;;
+        --exit-codes)
+            EXIT_CODES="$2"
+            shift 2
+            ;;
+        --generate-wrapper)
+            GENERATE_WRAPPER="$2"
+            shift 2
+            ;;
+        --target-script)
+            TARGET_SCRIPT="$2"
+            shift 2
+            ;;
+        *)
+            echo "Unknown argument: $1"
+            exit 1
+            ;;
+    esac
+done
+
+# Validate required arguments
+if [[ -z "${NAME:-}" ]]; then
+    echo "Error: --name is required"
+    exit 1
+fi
+if [[ -z "${DESCRIPTION:-}" ]]; then
+    echo "Error: --description is required"
+    exit 1
+fi
+if [[ -z "${ARGUMENTS:-}" ]]; then
+    echo "Error: --arguments is required"
+    exit 1
+fi
+if [[ -z "${USAGE_EXAMPLES:-}" ]]; then
+    echo "Error: --usage-examples is required"
+    exit 1
+fi
+if [[ -z "${FEATURES:-}" ]]; then
+    echo "Error: --features is required"
+    exit 1
+fi
+if [[ "${GENERATE_WRAPPER}" == "true" && -z "${TARGET_SCRIPT:-}" ]]; then
+    echo "Error: --target-script is required when --generate-wrapper is true"
+    exit 1
+fi
+
+# Set up paths
+COMMAND_MD_PATH=".roo/commands/${NAME}.md"
+WRAPPER_SH_PATH=".roo/commands/${NAME}.sh"
+
+# Read templates
+SKILL_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
+COMMAND_TEMPLATE="${SKILL_DIR}/assets/command-template.md"
+WRAPPER_TEMPLATE="${SKILL_DIR}/assets/wrapper-template.sh"
+
+# Generate Markdown file
+if [[ -f "${COMMAND_TEMPLATE}" ]]; then
+    # Prepare replacements
+    TITLE="${NAME//-/ }"  # Convert hyphens to spaces for title
+    TITLE="${TITLE^}"     # Capitalize first letter
+    LONG_DESCRIPTION="${DESCRIPTION}"
+    OPTIONS_LIST="${ARGUMENTS}"
+    FEATURES_LIST="${FEATURES}"
+
+    if [[ -n "${ENV_VARS:-}" ]]; then
+        ENV_VARS_LIST="${ENV_VARS}"
+    else
+        ENV_VARS_LIST="None"
+    fi
+
+    if [[ -n "${EXIT_CODES:-}" ]]; then
+        EXIT_CODES_LIST="${EXIT_CODES}"
+    else
+        EXIT_CODES_LIST="None"
+    fi
+
+    # Use sed with @ as delimiter to avoid conflicts with / in content
+    sed \
+        -e "s@{{description}}@${DESCRIPTION}@g" \
+        -e "s@{{arguments}}@${ARGUMENTS}@g" \
+        -e "s@{{title}}@${TITLE}@g" \
+        -e "s@{{long_description}}@${LONG_DESCRIPTION}@g" \
+        -e "s@{{name}}@${NAME}@g" \
+        -e "s@{{options_list}}@${OPTIONS_LIST}@g" \
+        -e "s@{{usage_examples}}@${USAGE_EXAMPLES}@g" \
+        -e "s@{{features_list}}@${FEATURES_LIST}@g" \
+        -e "s@{{env_vars_list}}@${ENV_VARS_LIST}@g" \
+        -e "s@{{exit_codes_list}}@${EXIT_CODES_LIST}@g" \
+        "${COMMAND_TEMPLATE}" > "${COMMAND_MD_PATH}"
+
+    echo "Generated slash command Markdown at ${COMMAND_MD_PATH}"
+else
+    echo "Error: Command template not found at ${COMMAND_TEMPLATE}"
+    exit 1
+fi
+
+# Generate wrapper script if requested
+if [[ "${GENERATE_WRAPPER}" == "true" ]]; then
+    if [[ -f "${WRAPPER_TEMPLATE}" ]]; then
+        # Use sed with @ as delimiter
+        sed \
+            -e "s@{{name}}@${NAME}@g" \
+            -e "s@{{target_script}}@${TARGET_SCRIPT}@g" \
+            "${WRAPPER_TEMPLATE}" > "${WRAPPER_SH_PATH}"
+
+        chmod +x "${WRAPPER_SH_PATH}"
+        echo "Generated wrapper script at ${WRAPPER_SH_PATH}"
+    else
+        echo "Error: Wrapper template not found at ${WRAPPER_TEMPLATE}"
+        exit 1
+    fi
+fi

-# Pull with rebase if behind
+# Sync repository state: stash changes, pull with rebase, then pop stash
+sync_repository_state() {
+    local branch="$1"
+    log_info "Syncing repository state for branch '$branch'..."
+    
+    # Check for uncommitted changes
+    local has_changes
+    if ! git_cmd_capture "git diff-index --quiet HEAD --"; then
+        has_changes=true
+        log_info "Uncommitted changes detected, stashing..."
+        if [[ "$DRY_RUN" == "true" ]]; then
+            log_info "[DRY RUN] Would run: git stash push -u -m \"auto-commit stash before sync\""
+        else
+            # Stash changes including untracked files
+            if ! git_cmd "git stash push -u -m \"auto-commit stash before sync\""; then
+                log_error "Failed to stash changes"
+                return 2
+            fi
+        fi
+    else
+        has_changes=false
+        log_info "No uncommitted changes found"
+    fi
+    
+    # Fetch latest
+    git_cmd "git fetch origin" >/dev/null
+    
+    # Check if behind
+    local local_hash
+    local remote_hash
+    local_hash=$(git_cmd "git rev-parse $branch")
+    remote_hash=$(git_cmd "git rev-parse origin/$branch")
+    
+    if [[ "$local_hash" != "$remote_hash" ]]; then
+        log_info "Branch is behind origin, performing pull --rebase..."
+        if [[ "$DRY_RUN" == "true" ]]; then
+            log_info "[DRY RUN] Would run: git pull --rebase origin $branch"
+        else
+            if ! git_cmd "git pull --rebase origin $branch"; then
+                log_error "Failed to pull --rebase"
+                # If we stashed changes, try to restore them before returning
+                if [[ "$has_changes" == "true" && "$DRY_RUN" != "true" ]]; then
+                    log_warn "Attempting to restore stashed changes after pull failure..."
+                    git_cmd "git stash pop" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
+                fi
+                return 5
+            fi
+        fi
+    else
+        log_info "Branch is up to date with origin"
+    fi
+    
+    # Pop stash if we had changes
+    if [[ "$has_changes" == "true" ]]; then
+        log_info "Restoring stashed changes..."
+        if [[ "$DRY_RUN" == "true" ]]; then
+            log_info "[DRY RUN] Would run: git stash pop"
+        else
+            if ! git_cmd "git stash pop"; then
+                log_warn "Conflicts occurred when popping stash - manual resolution may be needed"
+                # Don't return error here as the pull succeeded, just warn about conflicts
+            else
+                log_info "Stashed changes restored successfully"
+            fi
+        fi
+    fi
+    
+    log_info "Repository state synchronized"
+}

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# git-auto-commit wrapper - resolves workspace root and invokes skill script
+# Forwards all arguments, environment variables, and exit codes
+
+set -euo pipefail
+
+# Resolve workspace root relative to this wrapper
+SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
+WORKSPACE_ROOT="$(cd "${SCRIPT_DIR}/../.." && pwd)"
+
+# Path to the skill script
+SKILL_SCRIPT="${WORKSPACE_ROOT}/.roo/skills/git-auto-commit/scripts/git-auto-commit.sh"
+
+# Verify skill script exists
+if [[ ! -f "${SKILL_SCRIPT}" ]]; then
+    echo "Error: Skill script not found at ${SKILL_SCRIPT}" >&2
+    exit 1
+fi
+
+# Execute skill script with all arguments, forwarding environment
+# Use exec to replace current process and propagate exit code
+exec "${SKILL_SCRIPT}" "$@"

@@ -0,0 +1,147 @@
+# Consolidated Logging Design — OmniRoute Bandit Proxy
+
+## Summary of the problem
+
+The proxy currently emits multiple log lines per request because request logging is split across two Express middleware handlers and response/feedback logging is duplicated in both code paths (stream vs. non-stream). With `console` fully intercepted (each `console.log/error/warn` also writes to the in-memory `logBuffer` via `pushLog`), redundant lines are stored and surfaced by `/v1/logs` and the dashboard, cluttering the debug view.
+
+## Root causes (src/index.mjs)
+
+1. **Two middleware log the same incoming request** (duplicate `PROXY` + `DEBUG` line per request):
+   - Proxy log at [line 271](src/index.mjs:271): `console.log(`[PROXY] ${req.method} ${req.path}${suffix}`)` — logs all `/v1/*` API calls except polling routes.
+   - Debug log at [line 285](src/index.mjs:285): `console.log(`[DEBUG] Incoming request: ${req.method} ${req.path}`)` — logs **every** incoming request, unconditionally.
+2. **Loop-detection log fires twice** for the same detected loop (identical lines at [1130](src/index.mjs:1130) and [1135](src/index.mjs:1135)).
+3. **Response logging is repeated** in the non-stream path for tool-capable requests (lines [1645](src/index.mjs:1645) and [1647](src/index.mjs:1647)): one line for tool call count/content and a second line listing tool names.
+4. **Success lines are duplicated per code path** (stream at [1613](src/index.mjs:1613), non-stream at [1664](src/index.mjs:1664)) — near-identical `[SUCCESS]` lines emitted twice for the same request outcome.
+
+## Consolidation strategy
+
+**One source of truth: a single request entry log in the PROXY middleware.** The bare `[PROXY] GET /v1/chat/completions` / `[PROXY] POST /v1/chat/completions [TRAIN]` line becomes the canonical per-request identifier. Everything else is organized as:
+
+- `INFO` / `WARN`: per-request outcome and high-level state (model selected, retries exhausted, context rejects, upstream failures).
+- `DEBUG` (gateable behind `debugVerbose` and `/v1/debug/toggle`): request internals — headers, session key, tool details, per-attempt flow, raw errors.
+- `ERROR`: genuine failures — upstream errors, aborts, stream errors, rejection responses.
+- The existing `logBuffer` interception keeps all levels available to the `/v1/logs` API and dashboard.
+
+### Before / after: per-request log volume
+
+| Scenario | Before (lines) | After (lines) |
+|---|---|---|
+| Normal non-stream request | 2 (PROXY + DEBUG) + 1 SUCCESS + 2 RESPONSE (if tools) | 2 (PROXY + SUCCESS) |
+| Request rejected for context (413) | 2 (PROXY + DEBUG) + 1 WARN | 2 (PROXY + WARN) |
+| Request with loop / struggling | +2 redundant AFFINITY lines | +0 (single consolidated AFFINITY line) |
+| Stream success with tools | 2 (PROXY + DEBUG) + 1 SUCCESS + 1 RESPONSE-STREAM + 2 RESPONSE | 2 (PROXY + SUCCESS) + 1 RESPONSE-STREAM (DEBUG) |
+
+## Consolidated logging flow
+
+```mermaid
+flowchart TD
+    A[Incoming request] --> B{Express middleware}
+    B --> C[PROXY middleware: log one canonical line<br/>[PROXY] POST /v1/chat/completions suffix]
+    C --> D[Validation body guard<br/>400 if invalid]
+    D --> E[Token estimate + context cap check]
+    E --> F{estimated > MAX_CONTEXT_TOKENS?}
+    F -- yes / no auto-compress --> G{Re-check cap}
+    F -- yes / compress failed --> H{Still over cap}
+    H -- yes --> I[WARN [REJECT] 413]
+    H -- no --> J{mode / profile}
+    G -- no compress or compressed --> J
+    I --> K[send 413 response]
+    J --> L{requireTools?}
+    L -- yes --> M[INFO [TOOLS] tool-capable filter]
+    L -- no --> N[stream or non-stream path]
+    M --> N
+    N --> O{stream?}
+    O -- no --> P[non-stream path<br/>INFO [BANDIT] selected model<br/>INFO [SUCCESS] outcome<br/>ERROR on validation failure]
+    O -- yes --> Q[stream path<br/>INFO [BANDIT] selected model<br/>ERROR on stream abort<br/>INFO [SUCCESS] outcome]
+    P --> R[response.finish / close<br/>track end]
+    Q --> R
+    I --> R
+    K --> R
+    R --> S[console intercepted by pushLog<br/>→ logBuffer for /v1/logs]
+```
+
+## Middleware consolidation
+
+Replace the two separate middleware with a single, gateable handler (target ~lines 257–287 in `src/index.mjs`):
+
+```javascript
+// Single entry point: canonical per-request log + optional verbose body inspection
+app.use((req, res, next) => {
+  const isApi = req.path.startsWith("/v1/");
+  const isPolling = req.path.startsWith("/v1/metrics")
+    || req.path.startsWith("/v1/logs")
+    || req.path.startsWith("/v1/active")
+    || req.path.startsWith("/v1/modes")
+    || req.path.startsWith("/v1/models")
+    || req.path.startsWith("/v1/debug/status")
+    || req.path.startsWith("/v1/inflight");
+  if (isApi && !isPolling) {
+    let suffix = '';
+    if (req.method === 'POST' && req.path === '/v1/chat/completions') {
+      suffix = req.get('x-source') === 'training' ? ' [TRAIN]' : ' [ZOO]';
+    }
+    console.log(`[PROXY] ${req.method} ${req.path}${suffix}`);   // canonical, always on
+  }
+  if (isApi && !isPolling && debugVerbose) {
+    // verbose, on-demand: method + path + source + client
+    console.log(`[DEBUG] Incoming ${req.method} ${req.path} source=${req.get('x-source') || '-'}` +
+                ` client=${req.ip || req.connection?.remoteAddress || '?'}`);
+  }
+  next();
+});
+```
+
+This removes the unconditional `console.log(`[DEBUG] Incoming request…`)` (line 285) and keeps `[PROXY]` as the sole per-request log. Debug internals move behind `debugVerbose`.
+
+## Response/feedback consolidation
+
+- **Non-stream path** — remove lines 1645/1647 (duplicate `[RESPONSE]` lines). Tool-call details surface via the `[MSGS]`/`[MSGS-TOOL#]` logs (which are already `debugVerbose`-gated) and are optional to expose. If tool details must be visible at INFO level, emit a single consolidated line:
+  ```javascript
+  console.log(`[RESPONSE] ${model} tool_calls=${tc?.length || 0} names=${(tc || []).map(t => t.function?.name).join(", ")}`);
+  ```
+- **Success path** — keep exactly one `[SUCCESS]` line. The stream and non-stream variants differ only by `streamToolNames` vs `respToolNames`; consolidate to a helper (see below) called once per outcome.
+- **Loop detection** — remove the duplicate at line 1135; keep the first occurrence at line 1130.
+
+## Recommended log level mapping
+
+| Current tag | Level (proposed) | Gate | Rationale |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| `[PROXY]` (method/path) | INFO | always | Canonical per-request entry |
+| `[BANDIT] Selezionato` | INFO | always | Core routing outcome |
+| `[SUCCESS]` | INFO | always | Core outcome (replaces duplicate) |
+| `[AFFINITY] …` | INFO/WARN | always | Session management state |
+| `[FAILURE]` / `[UPSTREAM 4xx]` | ERROR | always | Actual failures |
+| `[REJECT]` / `[TIMEOUT]` | WARN | always | Recoverable but notable |
+| `[CONTEXT]` | WARN | always | Actions taken on request body |
+| `[RETRY]` | WARN | always | Retry/backoff events |
+| `[DEBUG] Incoming request`, `[DEBUG] verbose`, `[MSGS]`, `[MSGS-TOOL#]`, `[RESPONSE]`, `[RESPONSE-STREAM] tool_calls`, `[SESSION-KEY]`, `[FORCE]`, `[TOOLS]`, `[MODE]`, auto-compress internals | DEBUG | `debugVerbose` | Request internals, per-attempt flow |
+| `[AFFINITY] ⚠`, `[AFFINITY] 🚫`, `[AFFINITY] ⊕`, `[AFFINITY] ✗`, `[FALLBACK]` | INFO | always (or WARN for bans) | Important state changes |
+| `[BANDIT-TRAIN] …` (in `bandit.mjs`) | DEBUG | optional `DEBUG` env | Per-error-classification detail |
+
+All of these still pass through the `console.log/error/warn` overrides (lines 593–595) into `logBuffer`, so `/v1/logs` and the dashboard retain full visibility when polling is enabled.
+
+## Proposed helper functions
+
+Add near the logging overrides (after `pushLog`, before `startServer`) to centralize the repeated success message:
+
+```javascript
+// Consolidated request outcome log
+function logSuccess(model, dur, opts = {}) {
+  const { stream, toolNames, hasWritten, rewardScore, baseReward } = opts;
+  const tag = stream ? "[SUCCESS-STREAM]" : "[SUCCESS]";
+  console.log(`${tag} ${model} in ${dur.toFixed(2)}s ` +
+              `(reward: ${(rewardScore || 0).toFixed(3)} = base ${(baseReward || 0).toFixed(3)} ` +
+              `x ${(toolNames ? 0.6 : 1).toFixed(1)} tool=${toolNames?.[0] || 'none'} hasWritten=${hasWritten ?? '?'})`);
+}
+```
+
+Call once per completed request, and remove the duplicated lines at [1613](src/index.mjs:1613) and [1664](src/index.mjs:1664).
+
+## Implementation order
+
+1. Merge the two request middleware into the single gateable handler above (removes the 2× per-request line).
+2. Remove the duplicate loop-detection log (line 1135).
+3. Remove or consolidate the duplicate `[RESPONSE]` lines in the non-stream path (1645/1647).
+4. Introduce `logSuccess()` and consolidate stream/non-stream success logs (1613/1664).
+5. Re-map tag levels per the table above, keeping existing `debugVerbose` gates where present and adding them where absent (`[MSGS]`, `[MSGS-TOOL#]`, `[RESPONSE]`, `[RESPONSE-STREAM]`, `[SESSION-KEY]`, `[FORCE]`, `[TOOLS]`, `[MODE]`).
+6. Verify with `node --test` and a live proxy run: single `[PROXY]` line per request, `/v1/logs` clean, debug info toggleable via `/v1/debug/toggle?verbose=true`.

+# Reduce [DASHBOARD_STATS_DEBUG] Log Verbosity - Plan
+
+## Problem
+The `[DASHBOARD_STATS_DEBUG]` logs are repeating excessively, polluting the dashboard logs. Each poll of `/v1/dashboard/stats` triggers one log line: `isApi=true, isPolling=true, condition=false`.
+
+## Root Cause Analysis
+
+### 1. Log source (server-side)
+- **File**: `src/index.mjs`, lines 275-277
+- The Express middleware logs `[DASHBOARD_STATS_DEBUG]` on **every request** to `/v1/dashboard/stats`:
+```javascript
+if (req.path === '/v1/dashboard/stats') {
+  console.log(`[DASHBOARD_STATS_DEBUG] isApi=${isApi}, isPolling=${isPolling}, condition=${isApi && !isPolling}`);
+}
+```
+
+### 2. Request frequency (dashboard-side)
+- **File**: `public/dashboard.html`, line 2367
+- The dashboard polls `/v1/dashboard/stats` every **250ms**:
+```javascript
+setInterval(refreshAll, 250);
+```
+- This generates ~4 `[DASHBOARD_STATS_DEBUG]` logs per second, all identical (`isApi=true, isPolling=true, condition=false`).
+
+### 3. The log is diagnostic-only
+- The logged data (`isApi`, `isPolling`, `condition`) is derived from the request path, not actual bandit state
+- The meaningful dashboard stats (`totalRequests`, `avgReward`, etc.) are returned in the JSON response, not the log
+
+## Existing Precedent in Codebase
+
+The `/v1/models` endpoint uses a proven throttling pattern (`src/index.mjs:702-726`):
+```javascript
+const MODELS_LOG_THROTTLE_MS = parseInt(process.env.MODELS_LOG_THROTTLE_MS || "60000", 10);
+let modelsLogState = { lastLogAt: 0, suppressed: 0 };
+```
+
+## Proposed Solution: Change-Based Logging Throttling
+
+Implement a similar throttling state for `/v1/dashboard/stats` that only logs when the returned stats **actually change**, not on every poll.
+
+### Implementation Plan
+
+1. **Add throttle state after the `modelsLogState` definition** (around line 703)
+   - Track the last logged stats snapshot and suppressed request count
+
+2. **Modify the middleware at line 275-277** to:
+   - Generate a hash/summary of the stats data when logging
+   - Only log if data differs from last log
+   - Optionally add a maximum interval fallback (e.g., log at least every 60s)
+
+### Alternative Solutions Considered
+
+| Approach | Pros | Cons |
+|----------|------|------|
+| **Change-based throttling (RECOMMENDED)** | Keeps diagnostic info; reduces logs to meaningful state changes only | Slightly more complex |
+| **Time-based throttle (e.g., every 60s)** | Simple; consistent with `/v1/models` pattern | Less responsive to fast changes |
+| **Remove the log entirely** | Maximum verbosity reduction | Loses diagnostic capability |
+| **Switch to `console.debug`** | Logs hidden by default | Still generated; may clutter in debug mode |
+| **Reduce dashboard polling interval** | Reduces server load | Slower UI updates; requires frontend change |
+
+## Recommended Code Changes
+
+In `src/index.mjs`:
+
+**Line 275-277** (current):
+```javascript
+if (req.path === '/v1/dashboard/stats') {
+  console.log(`[DASHBOARD_STATS_DEBUG] isApi=${isApi}, isPolling=${isPolling}, condition=${isApi && !isPolling}`);
+}
+```
+
+**Line 275-277** (proposed):
+```javascript
+if (req.path === '/v1/dashboard/stats') {
+  const last = dashboardStatsLogState.lastLogAt || 0;
+  if (Date.now() - last >= DASHBOARD_STATS_LOG_INTERVAL_MS) {
+    dashboardStatsLogState.lastLogAt = Date.now();
+    dashboardStatsLogState.suppressed = 0;
+    console.log(`[DASHBOARD_STATS_DEBUG] isApi=${isApi}, isPolling=${isPolling}, condition=${isApi && !isPolling}`);
+  } else {
+    dashboardStatsLogState.suppressed++;
+  }
+}
+```
+
+**Configuration constant** (add near line 702, after `MODELS_LOG_THROTTLE_MS`):
+```javascript
+const DASHBOARD_STATS_LOG_INTERVAL_MS = parseInt(process.env.DASHBOARD_STATS_LOG_INTERVAL_MS || "60000", 10);
+let dashboardStatsLogState = { lastLogAt: 0, suppressed: 0 };
+```
+
+## Benefits
+
+1. **Dramatic verbosity reduction**: From ~4 logs/sec to ~1 log/min under normal conditions
+2. **Maintains diagnostics**: Logs still appear when needed for debugging
+3. **Configurable**: `DASHBOARD_STATS_LOG_INTERVAL_MS` env var allows tuning
+4. **Consistent**: Follows the existing `/v1/models` throttling pattern in the codebase
+5. **No frontend change required**: Dashboard polling interval (250ms) remains unchanged
+
+## Validation Steps
+
+After implementation, verify:
+1. Server restarts without syntax errors
+2. Dashboard continues to update with correct stats
+3. `[DASHBOARD_STATS_DEBUG]` logs appear at the configured interval (default 60s)
+4. Logs can be enabled more frequently by setting `DASHBOARD_STATS_LOG_INTERVAL_MS`

+// ========================================
+// VALIDAZIONE RISPOSTA

+function validateNonStreamResponse(data, opts = {}) {
+  const requireTools = opts.requireTools === true;
+  if (!data || typeof data !== "object") return "empty response body";
+
+  // Errori espliciti ovunque nel body
+  if (data.error) return "body.error: " + (data.error.message || JSON.stringify(data.error).slice(0, 100));
+  if (data.code && data.code >= 400) return "body.code: " + data.code;
+  if (data.type === "error") return "body.type=error";
+
+  // Struttura choices
+  if (!Array.isArray(data.choices) || data.choices.length === 0) return "no choices";
+
+  const ch = data.choices[0];
+  if (!ch || !ch.message) return "no message in choice[0]";
+
+  // Contenuto vuoto (né content né tool_calls né reasoning)
+  const content = ch.message.content;
+  const toolCalls = ch.message.tool_calls;
+  const reasoning = ch.message.reasoning_content || ch.message.reasoning;
+
+  const hasText = typeof content === "string" && content.trim().length > 0;
+  const hasTools = Array.isArray(toolCalls) && toolCalls.length > 0;
+  const hasReasoning = typeof reasoning === "string" && reasoning.trim().length > 0;
+
+  if (!hasText && !hasTools) {
+    // Se ha solo reasoning, è un reasoning model troncato (max_tokens)
+    if (hasReasoning) return "only reasoning, no content (max_tokens too low?)";
+    return "empty content";
+  }
+
+  // Finish reason anomali
+  const fr = ch.finish_reason;
+  if (fr === "content_filter") return "content_filter";
+  // "length" è ok se ha contenuto; è solo un warning
+
+    // Rileva "errore" mascherato da risposta normale (200 OK con contenuto di avviso)
+  if (typeof content === "string" && /run out of usage|out of credits|quota exceeded|insufficient.*balance|upgrade.*plan/i.test(content)) {
+    return "provider-quota-exceeded: " + content.slice(0, 100);
+  }
+  // === Se la richiesta aveva tools, il modello DEVE aver chiamato almeno un tool ===
+  if (requireTools && !hasTools) {
+    // Eccezione: se il modello ha esplicitamente rifiutato, non è colpa sua
+    const t = (content || "").toLowerCase();
+    const legitRefusal = /(non posso|cannot|can't|not able|refuse|sorry.*can't)/i.test(t);
+    if (!legitRefusal) {
+      return "no-tool-call-but-required (model ignored tools)";
+    }
+  }
+  
+  return null;  // valida
+}

+function validateStreamAccumulated(raw, opts = {}) {
+  const requireTools = opts.requireTools === true;
+            // DEBUG risposta stream
+            if (requireTools) {
+              const toolCallMatches = raw.match(/"tool_calls"/g);
+              const toolNames = [...raw.matchAll(/"name"\s*:\s*"([^"]+)"/g)].map(m => m[1]).slice(0, 5);
+              console.log(`[RESPONSE-STREAM] tool_calls found: ${toolCallMatches?.length || 0} | names: ${toolNames.join(", ")}`);
+            }
+  if (!raw || raw.length === 0) return "empty stream";
+    if (/^\s*data:\s*\{\s*"error"/m.test(raw)) {
+      // Estrai la riga data: che contiene "error" — NON la prima riga data: {...}
+      // (il primo data: può essere un keepalive con delta vuoto)
+      let payload = "";
+      for (const line of raw.split("\n")) {
+        const t = line.trim();
+        if (t.startsWith("data:") && t.includes('"error"')) {
+          payload = t.slice(5).trim();
+          break;
+        }
+      }
+      if (!payload) payload = raw.slice(0, 2000);
+
+      let innerMessage = "";
+      let status = 0;
+      let code = "";
+      try {
+        const parsed = JSON.parse(payload);
+        const errObj = parsed.error || {};
+        innerMessage = errObj.message || "";
+        code = errObj.code || "";
+        if (code === "model_shutdown") status = 410;
+        else if (code === "model_not_found") status = 400;
+        else if (/unknown provider for model|not supported|model_not_found/i.test(innerMessage)) status = 400;
+        else if (/does not exist|not found|no longer available/i.test(innerMessage)) status = 404;
+        else if (/quota|rate limit/i.test(innerMessage)) status = 429;
+      } catch (_) {}
+      console.error(`[SSE ERROR RAW] ${payload.slice(0, 600)}`);
+      return { reason: "SSE contains error", status, message: innerMessage || payload.slice(0, 500) };
+    }
+  // Estrai l'ultimo data: {...} utile e verifica se ha contenuto
+  const lines = raw.split("\n").filter(l => l.startsWith("data: "));
+  if (lines.length === 0) return "no SSE data lines";
+
+  let hasContent = false;
+  let hasTools = false;
+  for (const line of lines) {
+    const json = line.slice(6).trim();
+    if (json === "[DONE]") continue;
+    try {
+      const obj = JSON.parse(json);
+      if (obj.error) return "SSE chunk error: " + (obj.error.message || "").slice(0, 100);
+      const delta = obj.choices?.[0]?.delta;
+      if (!delta) continue;
+      if (typeof delta.content === "string" && delta.content.length > 0) hasContent = true;
+      if (Array.isArray(delta.tool_calls) && delta.tool_calls.length > 0) hasTools = true;
+    } catch {}
+  }
+  if (requireTools && !hasTools) {
+    // Controlla se c'è stato un rifiuto legittimo nel testo accumulato
+    const legitRefusal = /(non posso|cannot|can't|not able|refuse)/i.test(raw);
+    if (!legitRefusal) {
+      return "no-tool-call-but-required (model ignored tools)";
+    }
+  }
+
+  if (!hasContent && !hasTools) return "stream has no content nor tool_calls";
+  return null;  // valida
+}
+// Compressione d'emergenza: pochi messaggi ma uno è enorme (system/env_details).
+// Tronca il messaggio più grande finché il totale scende sotto targetTokens.
+function truncateBiggestMessage(body, targetTokens) {
+  if (!body || typeof body !== "object") return null;
+  const messages = body.messages;
+  if (!Array.isArray(messages) || messages.length === 0) return null;
+
+  const msgText = (m) => {
+    if (typeof m.content === "string") return m.content;
+    if (Array.isArray(m.content)) return m.content.map(p => p?.text || "").join("\n");
+    return JSON.stringify(m.content || "");
+  };
+  const msgTokens = (m) => Math.ceil(msgText(m).length / 3);
+
+  // Trova il messaggio più grande
+  let idx = 0;
+  for (let k = 1; k < messages.length; k++) {
+    if (msgTokens(messages[k]) > msgTokens(messages[idx])) idx = k;
+  }
+  const big = messages[idx];
+  const bigText = msgText(big);
+  const bigTokens = msgTokens(big);
+
+  // Se è già piccolo, non c'è nulla da tagliare
+  if (bigTokens < 2000) return null;
+
+  // Calcola quanti char tenere: proporzione rispetto al target
+  const totalTokens = messages.reduce((s, m) => s + msgTokens(m), 0);
+  const keepRatio = Math.max(0.15, Math.min(0.9, targetTokens / Math.max(1, totalTokens)));
+  const keepChars = Math.max(2000, Math.ceil(bigText.length * keepRatio));
+  const removedChars = bigText.length - keepChars;
+  const removedTokens = Math.ceil(removedChars / 3);
+
+  const truncated = bigText.slice(0, keepChars)
+    + `\n\n[... troncato: ${removedTokens} token rimossi per limite contesto ...]`;
+
+  const newMsg = Array.isArray(big.content)
+    ? { ...big, content: [{ type: "text", text: truncated }] }
+    : { ...big, content: truncated };
+
+  const newMessages = messages.slice();
+  newMessages[idx] = newMsg;
+  const newBody = { ...body, messages: newMessages };
+  return { body: newBody, omitted: 0, truncatedBig: true, removedTokens };
+}
+// ========================================
+// CONTEXT COMPRESSION (sliding window per agent di coding)
+// ========================================
+// Mantiene: system + primo user + ultimi N messaggi.
+// Rispetta i confini dei blocchi tool_call/tool result (non li spezza mai).
+function compressBody(body, targetTokens) {
+  if (!body || typeof body !== "object") return null;
+  const messages = body.messages;
+  if (!Array.isArray(messages) || messages.length === 0) return null;
+  // Con pochi messaggi (2-5), la compressione strutturale non ha nulla da rimuovere.
+  // Tronca direttamente il messaggio più grande.
+  if (messages.length < 6) {
+    return truncateBiggestMessage(body, targetTokens);
+  }
+  // 1. Prendi system + primo user (parte "fissa")
+  const head = [];
+  let i = 0;
+  while (i < messages.length && messages[i].role === "system") {
+    head.push(messages[i]);
+    i++;
+  }
+  if (i < messages.length && messages[i].role === "user") {
+    head.push(messages[i]);
+    i++;
+  }
+
+  // 2. Trova un boundary sicuro per la coda:
+  //    non deve iniziare con un "tool" orfano (deve essere user o assistant senza tool_calls pendenti).
+  const TAIL_TARGET = 8;
+  let tailStart = Math.max(i, messages.length - TAIL_TARGET);
+  while (tailStart > i && tailStart < messages.length) {
+    const m = messages[tailStart];
+    if (m.role === "user" || (m.role === "assistant" && !m.tool_calls)) break;
+    tailStart++;
+  }
+  // Se ci siamo spostati troppo avanti, non è comprimibile in modo sicuro
+  if (tailStart >= messages.length - 1) return null;
+  if (tailStart <= i) return null;
+
+  // 3. Verifica che head non finisca con un assistant con tool_calls (orfano)
+  //    Se sì, rimuovi l'ultimo elemento di head.
+  while (head.length > 0 && head[head.length - 1].role === "assistant" && head[head.length - 1].tool_calls) {
+    head.pop();
+  }
+
+  const tail = messages.slice(tailStart);
+  const omitted = tailStart - i;
+
+  const compressed = [
+    ...head,
+    {
+      role: "user",
+      content: `[Sistema: ${omitted} messaggi intermedi omessi per ridurre il contesto. Se hai bisogno di dettagli su passaggi precedenti, chiedili esplicitamente.]`
+    },
+    ...tail
+  ];
+
+  const newBody = { ...body, messages: compressed };
+  // Verifica dimensione risultante
+  const s = JSON.stringify(newBody);
+  const newTokens = Math.ceil(s.length / 3);
+  if (newTokens > targetTokens) return null;
+
+  return { body: newBody, omitted };
+}

+// ========================================
+// RING BUFFER PER LOG CIRCOLARI
+// ========================================
+
+class RingBuffer {
+  constructor(maxSize) {
+    this.maxSize = maxSize;
+    this.buffer = [];
+    this.index = 0;
+  }
+
+  push(item) {
+    if (this.buffer.length < this.maxSize) {
+      this.buffer.push(item);
+    } else {
+      this.buffer[this.index] = item;
+      this.index = (this.index + 1) % this.maxSize;
+    }
+  }
+
+  getAll() {
+    if (this.buffer.length < this.maxSize) {
+      return [...this.buffer];
+    }
+    return [...this.buffer.slice(this.index), ...this.buffer.slice(0, this.index)];
+  }
+}

+const sessionBlacklist = new Map();

+function computeSessionKey(messages) {
+  if (!Array.isArray(messages) || messages.length === 0) return null;
+
+  // Prendi il system prompt (o, se manca, il primo user message)
+  const sys = messages.find(m => m.role === "system");
+  const firstUser = messages.find(m => m.role === "user");
+
+  const sysStr = sys
+    ? (typeof sys.content === "string" ? sys.content : JSON.stringify(sys.content))
+    : "";
+  const userStr = firstUser
+    ? (typeof firstUser.content === "string" ? firstUser.content : JSON.stringify(firstUser.content))
+    : "";
+
+  // 🎯 Usa SOLO il prefisso stabile:
+  // - system: primi 800 char (l'header "You are Zoo..." è lì)
+  // - user:   primi 300 char (la richiesta originale dell'utente è lì)
+  // Tutto ciò che viene dopo è contesto dinamico che cambia ad ogni turno.
+  const stableSys  = sysStr.slice(0, 800);
+  const stableUser = userStr.slice(0, 300);
+
+  if (!stableSys && !stableUser) return null;
+
+  return createHash("md5")
+    .update(stableSys + "|" + stableUser)
+    .digest("hex")
+    .slice(0, 16);
+}

+let requestCounter = 0;
+function newRequestId() {
+  return `req-${Date.now()}-${++requestCounter}`;
+}
+// Moltiplicatore reward basato sul tipo di tool chiamato.
+// I modelli che rispondono con "ask_followup_question" invece di agire
+// prendono reward bassi → UCB1 li declassa.
+function computeToolRewardMultiplier(toolNames, hasWrittenInSession) {
+  if (!toolNames || toolNames.length === 0) return 0.6;
+  const first = String(toolNames[0] || '').toLowerCase();
+
+  if (first === 'ask_followup_question') return 0.5;
+  if (first === 'update_todo_list') return 0.8;
+
+  // attempt_completion senza mai aver scritto → conclusione prematura
+  if (first === 'attempt_completion') {
+    return hasWrittenInSession ? 1.0 : 0.3;
+  }
+
+  // Delegare ad un'altra mode è sempre un'azione valida
+  if (first === 'new_task') return 1.0;
+
+  // Tool di scrittura/modifica: reward pieno
+  const writeTools = ['apply_diff','write_to_file','replace_in_file',
+                      'execute_command','insert_content'];
+  if (writeTools.includes(first)) return 1.0;
+
+  // Tool di lettura/ricerca: neutro
+  const readTools = ['read_file','list_files','search_files','codebase_search'];
+  if (readTools.includes(first)) return 1.0;
+
+  return 0.9;
+}
+
+// Ritorna true se almeno un assistant message nella history ha chiamato
+// un tool di scrittura. Serve per capire se attempt_completion è prematuro.
+function sessionHasWritten(messages) {
+  const writeTools = new Set(['apply_diff','write_to_file','replace_in_file',
+                              'execute_command','insert_content']);
+  const msgs = messages || [];
+
+  // Pass 1: raccogli gli id dei tool_call di scrittura
+  const writeCallIds = new Set();
+  for (const m of msgs) {
+    if (m.role !== 'assistant' || !Array.isArray(m.tool_calls)) continue;
+    for (const tc of m.tool_calls) {
+      const name = (tc.function?.name || tc.name || '').toLowerCase();
+      if (writeTools.has(name) && tc.id) writeCallIds.add(tc.id);
+    }
+  }
+
+  // Fallback legacy: nessun id → comportamento originale (qualsiasi write call → true)
+  if (writeCallIds.size === 0) {
+    for (const m of msgs) {
+      if (m.role !== 'assistant' || !Array.isArray(m.tool_calls)) continue;
+      for (const tc of m.tool_calls) {
+        const name = (tc.function?.name || tc.name || '').toLowerCase();
+        if (writeTools.has(name)) return true;
+      }
+    }
+    return false;
+  }
+
+  // Pass 2: cerca i tool_result associati e marca quelli falliti
+  const FAIL_RE = /unable to apply all diff|unable to apply any part|no sufficiently similar|edit unsuccessful/i;
+  const failedIds = new Set();
+  for (const m of msgs) {
+    if (m.role !== 'tool') continue;
+    const id = m.tool_call_id || m.toolCallId;
+    if (!id || !writeCallIds.has(id)) continue;
+    const c = typeof m.content === 'string' ? m.content : JSON.stringify(m.content || '');
+    if (FAIL_RE.test(c)) failedIds.add(id);
+  }
+
+  // True se almeno un write call NON è fallito
+  for (const id of writeCallIds) {
+    if (!failedIds.has(id)) return true;
+  }
+  return false;
+}
+function trackRequestStart(id, meta) {
+  activeRequests.set(id, {
+    source: meta.source || 'zoo',
+    id,
+    startTime: Date.now(),
+    ...meta
+  });
+}
+
+function trackRequestUpdate(id, patch) {
+  const r = activeRequests.get(id);
+  if (r) Object.assign(r, patch);
+}
+
+function trackRequestEnd(id) {
+  activeRequests.delete(id);
+}
+
+function getActiveRequestsSnapshot() {
+  const now = Date.now();
+  return Array.from(activeRequests.values()).map(r => {
+    const info = r.model ? bandit.getModelInfo(r.model) : null;
+    const rank = r.model ? bandit.getModelRank(r.model) : null;
+    return {
+      ...r,
+      elapsedMs: now - r.startTime,
+      elapsedSec: Math.round((now - r.startTime) / 100) / 10,
+      N: info?.N ?? null,
+      avg: info?.avg ?? null,
+      trend: info?.trend ?? 'flat',
+      rank,
+    };
+  }).sort((a, b) => b.startTime - a.startTime);
+}
+
+// Ultime richieste completate (per mostrare activity quando idle)
+const recentRequests = new RingBuffer(5);
+
+function trackRequestComplete(id, meta) {
+  const r = activeRequests.get(id);
+  if (r) {
+    const info = r.model ? bandit.getModelInfo(r.model) : null;
+    const rank = r.model ? bandit.getModelRank(r.model) : null;
+    recentRequests.push({
+      ...r,
+      ...meta,
+      endedAt: Date.now(),
+      durationSec: Math.round((Date.now() - r.startTime) / 100) / 10,
+      N: info?.N ?? null,
+      avg: info?.avg ?? null,
+      trend: info?.trend ?? 'flat',
+      rank,
+    });
+  }
+}
+
+// ========================================
+// CONSOLE OVERRIDE CON TRUNCATURA
+// ========================================
+
+const originalLog = console.log;
+const originalError = console.error;
+const originalWarn = console.warn;
+
+function serializeArgs(args) {
+  return args.map(arg => {
+    if (typeof arg === "string") return arg;
+    if (arg instanceof Error) return arg.stack || arg.message;
+    try {
+      const str = JSON.stringify(arg);
+      return str && str.length > 1000 ? str.substring(0, 1000) + "... (truncated)" : str;
+    } catch {
+      return String(arg);
+    }
+  }).join(" ");
+}
+
+console.log = (...args) => { originalLog(...args); pushLog(serializeArgs(args)); };
+console.error = (...args) => { originalError(...args); pushLog("ERROR: " + serializeArgs(args)); };
+console.warn = (...args) => { originalWarn(...args); pushLog("WARN: " + serializeArgs(args)); };

+      return res.status(400).json({ error: { message: "Missing required fields" } });
+    }
+  }
+  next();
+});

+app.get("/v1/scripts", requireAuth, (req, res) => {
+  try {
+    const scriptsDir = path.join(__dirname, "../scripts");
+    const files = fs.readdirSync(scriptsDir);
+    const scripts = files
+      .filter(f => f.endsWith('.mjs') || f.endsWith('.sh'))
+      .map(f => {
+        const fullPath = path.join(scriptsDir, f);
+        const stats = fs.statSync(fullPath);
+        return {
+          name: f,
+          path: fullPath,
+          size: stats.size,
+          modified: stats.mtime.toISOString(),
+          isExecutable: (stats.mode & 0o111) !== 0,
+          type: f.endsWith('.mjs') ? 'javascript' : 'shell'
+        };
+      });
+    res.json({ scripts });
+  } catch (e) {
+    console.error("[API] Errore lettura script:", e.message);
+    res.status(500).json({ error: e.message });
+  }
+});
+
+app.post("/v1/scripts/execute", requireAuth, express.json(), (req, res) => {
+  try {
+    const { scriptPath, args = [] } = req.body || {};
+    if (!scriptPath) {
+      return res.status(400).json({ error: "scriptPath richiesto" });
+    }
+    
+    // Validazione del percorso per prevenire path traversal
+    const scriptsDir = path.join(__dirname, "../scripts");
+    const normalizedPath = path.normalize(scriptPath);
+    const absolutePath = path.join(scriptsDir, normalizedPath);
+    
+    if (!absolutePath.startsWith(scriptsDir)) {
+      return res.status(403).json({ error: "Percorso non autorizzato" });
+    }
+    
+    if (!fs.existsSync(absolutePath)) {
+      return res.status(404).json({ error: "Script non trovato" });
+    }
+    
+    // Esecuzione dello script
+    const spawn = require("child_process").spawn;
+    const isShell = absolutePath.endsWith('.sh');
+    
+    let command, options;
+    if (isShell) {
+      command = "bash";
+      options = { shell: true };
+    } else {
+      command = "node";
+      options = {};
+    }
+    
+    const child = spawn(command, [absolutePath, ...args], {
+      cwd: scriptsDir,
+      stdio: ["pipe", "pipe", "pipe"],
+      ...options
+    });
+    
+    const output = {
+      pid: child.pid,
+      command: `${command} ${absolutePath} ${args.join(' ')}`,
+      startTime: Date.now(),
+      status: "running"
+    };
+    
+    let stdoutData = "";
+    let stderrData = "";
+    
+    child.stdout?.on("data", (data) => {
+      stdoutData += data.toString();
+    });
+    
+    child.stderr?.on("data", (data) => {
+      stderrData += data.toString();
+    });
+    
+    child.on("close", (code) => {
+      output.status = "completed";
+      output.exitCode = code;
+      output.stdout = stdoutData;
+      output.stderr = stderrData;
+      output.endTime = Date.now();
+      output.duration = output.endTime - output.startTime;
+      
+      // Salva l'output in un file per riferimento
+      const outputFile = path.join(scriptsDir, `.script-output-${child.pid}.json`);
+      fs.writeFileSync(outputFile, JSON.stringify(output, null, 2));
+    });
+    
+    res.json(output);
+  } catch (e) {
+    console.error("[API] Errore esecuzione script:", e.message);
+    res.status(500).json({ error: e.message });
+  }
+});
+
+app.get("/v1/scripts/output/:pid", requireAuth, (req, res) => {
+  try {
+    const { pid } = req.params;
+    const scriptsDir = path.join(__dirname, "../scripts");
+    const outputFile = path.join(scriptsDir, `.script-output-${pid}.json`);
+    
+    if (!fs.existsSync(outputFile)) {
+      return res.status(404).json({ error: "Output script non trovato" });
+    }
+    
+    const output = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(outputFile, "utf8"));
+    res.json(output);
+  } catch (e) {
+    console.error("[API] Errore lettura output script:", e.message);
+    res.status(500).json({ error: e.message });
+  }
+});
